The chorus repeats, so learn it first. Then the verses will connect around it.
That helps a lot. I'll start with the chorus.
Good. Record yourself singing, and listen for places where you hesitate. Those are the lines to practise next.
I will. It's such a fun song.
Then enjoy it. Learning a song you love never feels like work.
My parents say I spend too much time on my phone. I think it's not that much.
That's a common difference between parents and teenagers. How many hours do you spend on it each day?
Maybe three or four hours, mostly after school.
That's a lot for someone with school work. Your parents may worry that it takes time from sleep, hobbies and family.
But it's how I talk to my friends.
That's a fair point. You could suggest a plan: set times for studying and family, and allow time for friends. Showing them you can balance it will earn their trust.
I'm scared to ask my professor a question because I think it's silly.
Most professors enjoy questions, and no honest question is silly. Chances are that others in the class wonder the same thing.
What if he thinks I wasn't listening?
Try asking it in a way that shows you've thought about it: 'I understood this part, but I'm not clear about that part.' That shows effort.
My best friend's birthday is next Friday, and I want to find a gift she'll really like.
Think about what she talks about or uses a lot. What does she enjoy?
She loves reading and drawing.
Then a nice sketchbook and a set of pencils, or a book from an author she likes, would be great.
She already has lots of books.
Then art supplies might be better. A small set of good pencils and a sketchbook could be exciting, as she can use them.
Should I wrap it?
Yes. Add a handwritten note about something you like about her. That makes the gift feel personal.
Our lane wants to put on a small street play about keeping the area clean. I'm supposed to write the script.
That's a great way to share a message. Keep it short, around ten minutes, with simple scenes and a few characters.
What should the story be?
Maybe a person who throws litter and meets a funny 'garbage monster' who shows the effect of mess. It can be humorous but have a clear point at the end.
I'm joining a new school in the middle of the year and I don't know anyone.
That's a big change, and it's normal to feel nervous. The first days are the hardest. What are you most worried about?
Eating alone at lunch.
Try to introduce yourself to one or two classmates on the first day. A simple 'Hi, I'm new. Can I sit here?' works. Most children are kind to new students.
What if no one talks to me?
Give it a few days. People take time to warm up. Join an activity like a club or sports period, where you can meet others with the same interests.
I like drawing.
Then look for an art club or ask the art teacher. Sharing a hobby is a natural way to make friends.
That gives me something to look forward to.
Good. Bring a small sketchbook on the first day, and it might start a conversation.
My grandmother knows many old folk songs and I'd like to learn them from her.
What a precious thing to do. Songs like these are often not written down, so learning them keeps them alive.
Should I record her?
Ask her permission first. If she agrees, a phone recording is handy. You could also write the words in a notebook as she sings.
Texting or calling? Me and my friend disagree. I like texting and she likes calling. It's causing problems.
That can cause misunderstandings. What happens?
She says texting feels cold, and I say calls feel like too much.
Both feelings are valid. You could meet halfway: text during the week and have a longer call on weekends.
She would probably like that.
Then tell her it's because you care and want to stay close. Explaining your reason helps her not take it personally.
I'll suggest it tonight.
Good. Being open about it shows you value the friendship, and that matters more than the method.
We have guests coming, some vegetarian and some who eat non-vegetarian food. How do I plan the menu?
Make a menu where the main parts work for everyone, such as rice, dal, a vegetable dish and salad. Then add one or two non-vegetarian dishes as extras.
Should I cook them separately?
Yes, use separate pans and spoons for each, so the vegetarian dishes stay free of meat. Label the dishes if you set up a buffet.
What about dessert?
A vegetarian dessert like kheer or fruit salad suits everyone. Check if anyone has allergies, such as to nuts.
I'll ask them when I invite them.
Good. Asking early gives you time to adjust.
This makes me feel much calmer about it.
Plan the cooking order too, so that the dishes that can be made ahead are ready first.
Is it better to sit by the window or the aisle on a long journey?
It depends on what you want. The window gives you a view and something to lean on when sleeping.
And the aisle?
The aisle lets you stand up and stretch without disturbing others. Many people prefer it for long trips.
My office is so noisy that I can't focus.
That's tough. Is the noise from people talking or from machines?
Mostly people chatting and phone calls.
Headphones, even without music, can lower the noise a little. Or you could find a quiet corner or meeting room for tasks that need focus.
My boss doesn't like headphones.
Then maybe ask him if you can use a quiet room for an hour or two each day. Say it's to do your best work on difficult tasks.
I'm learning to skip rope and I keep tripping.
That happens at the start. Make sure the rope is the right length: standing on its middle, the handles should reach your armpits.
I jump too high, I think.
Yes, small hops just above the ground are enough. Keep your elbows near your body and turn the rope with your wrists.
I got a low mark in science today and I feel awful.
I'm sorry. That feels bad, especially when you studied. Did you expect a different result?
Yes, I thought I did well.
That is disappointing. Look at the paper to see where you lost marks. Sometimes it's a misread question rather than not knowing the topic.
What if my parents get upset?
Tell them yourself and show that you're ready to improve. Parents often respond better when they see you take it seriously.
I feel better. I'll ask my teacher about it.
Good. Asking the teacher shows you care about learning, and she can point out what to improve.
Thanks for listening.
Anytime. One test doesn't decide how you do in the long run.
I just got a 500-piece jigsaw puzzle and I'm overwhelmed by all those pieces.
Start with the edges. Find all the straight-sided pieces and build the frame first.
Then what?
Sort the rest by colour or pattern. Work on one section at a time, like the sky or a building, and join the sections later.
I want to collect fallen leaves in autumn and make a scrapbook.
A lovely idea. Pick leaves that are dry and not crumbly, and press them between pages of a heavy book for a week or two.
Then what?
Glue them onto thick paper, and label each with the tree's name, if you know it, and the date and place you found it.
What if I don't know the tree?
Take a photo of the whole tree and look it up in a plant guide or ask someone at a garden. Learning the names is half the fun.
I usually read mysteries. Do you think I should try something different, like a biography?
Trying something new can be refreshing. A biography is a true story, so it reads differently, but a good one has twists like a mystery.
Whose life should I read about?
Pick someone whose work or story already interests you, such as a scientist, a sportsperson or a social reformer. A shorter book is a good way to start.
Okay, but I'll still read my mysteries too.
Of course. Reading different types makes you a stronger reader, and you don't have to give up what you love.
My grandfather's eyes are weak now and he can't read his newspapers. I want to read to him.
That is a kind thing to do. Reading aloud together can become a daily habit that you both enjoy.
What should I read?
Start with the news items that he likes, such as local stories, then add short stories or a chapter from a book he loves.
I read too fast and he says he can't follow.
Slow down and pause at the end of each sentence. A calm voice is easier to listen to than a hurried one.
Should I explain difficult words?
Only if he asks. You can always stop and talk about a story after it ends, and that's often what grandparents enjoy most.
He will like that. He always tells me old stories.
Then you might hear a story behind every news item. Enjoy the time, and maybe take notes of his stories.
Our school library has started a reading challenge. We must read ten books by December.
That is a fun challenge. Ten books in a few months is doable if you plan it. How much do you read now?
About one book a month.
Then pick shorter books to start and read twenty minutes a day. A small daily habit adds up quickly.
What if I get bored of a book?
It's fine to swap it for another, as long as you finish enough in total. Keep a list of books you want to try in case you need a quick replacement.
Can I count comics?
Ask your librarian. Many libraries allow comics or picture books, but some count only novels, so check the rules.
I can't find my bookmark and I always forget my page.
A bookmark is easy to replace. Use a thin strip of card, a ribbon or an old postcard.
Folding the page corner is quicker.
It is, but it can damage the paper over time, especially in library books. A slip of paper works just as well and doesn't hurt the book.
Fair enough. I'll cut one from an old envelope.
That's perfect. You can decorate it with a drawing if you like.
For Holi this year, our colony would like to save water. Do you have ideas?
Yes, use dry colours instead of wet ones, and stay away from water balloons and hoses. Natural colours are gentler on the soil, too.
But the children love the water guns.
You could set aside a small area for them, with a limited supply from one bucket, and encourage them to refill only when needed. It keeps the fun and cuts waste.
Two new families moved into our building and I'd like to make them feel welcome.
A friendly gesture goes a long way. You could knock on their door, introduce yourself and offer help with directions or local shops.
Should I bring food?
A small plate of homemade sweets or snacks is a lovely gesture. Check first if they have any food restrictions.
What if they're shy?
Keep the visit short and warm, and don't push for a long chat. Say you're a neighbour if they need anything. They'll remember your kindness.
I'll go on Sunday afternoon, then.
A good time, since people are usually at home and relaxed. Let them settle in for a few days first.
A group of us wants to clean the lakeside near our town on Sunday. It's really dirty.
That's a great initiative. Plan it well, so the day goes smoothly. How many people are joining?
About fifteen.
Good number. Bring strong gloves, garbage bags and sticks for picking up litter. Wear closed shoes and keep an eye out for sharp objects.
What should we do with all the waste?
Ask your local municipality in advance to collect it, or arrange a vehicle to take it to the proper place. Separate plastic from other waste if you can.
Should we take our kids?
Older children can help in safe areas, but keep young ones away from the water's edge. Assign an adult to watch them.
We'll plan that. Thanks.
Good luck. Take before and after photos, and share them. They can inspire others to join the next time.
Our building's notice board is a mess. Papers are stuck everywhere.
A tidy board is easier to read. You could ask the committee if you can sort it out.
What would we do?
Remove old notices, create sections such as events, rules and lost items, and give each a clear label. Set a date on each notice so they are removed on time.
Good, I'll talk to the secretary.
Great. Offer to check the board once a week, and the system will last.
Our house is full of old newspapers piling up. Mom wants me to deal with them.
A good chore to tackle. Do you have a place to give or sell them?
The raddiwala comes on Saturdays.
Then tie them in bundles and keep them ready for him. If there are some interesting articles you want to keep, cut them out first.
My room gets so warm in the afternoon. How can I make it cooler?
Close the curtains or blinds on the sunny side to keep the heat out. Open windows in the evening when the air outside cools down.
I only have a ceiling fan.
It still helps. Make sure it runs in the right direction, and place a bowl of cold water or damp cloth near it, which can make the air feel cooler.
Is it okay to sleep with a wet cloth on the window?
Hanging a damp cloth on the window can cool the incoming air a little, as the water evaporates. Keep it away from electric points.
We'll try that. Thanks.
Also wear light cotton clothes, and keep a water bottle nearby.
A little plant corner in the living room is my plan. Where do I begin?
Choose a spot near a window with soft light. Then pick a few easy plants like money plant, snake plant or pothos.
Is there anything I should avoid?
Avoid placing plants in direct hot sun behind glass, and don't leave water sitting in saucers, since it can rot the roots.
What about the pots?
Any pot with a hole at the bottom works. If it's a decorative pot without holes, keep the plant in a plastic pot inside it.
I have a few old cups too.
Those make charming little planters, as long as you make a drainage hole in the bottom. Ask an adult to help if the cup is hard.
Good idea. I'll start this weekend.
Take it slowly with watering. Check the soil with your finger before adding more.
My little sister wants a night light in her room. Which kind is best?
A soft, warm-coloured light that she can switch off easily is ideal. It gives comfort without keeping her awake.
Should it be bright?
No, dim is enough. Too much light can make it harder to sleep.
What if she wants a character one?
That's fine as long as it's from a safe, well-made product with covered parts. Let her choose, because she'll feel more secure with something she loves.
Tomorrow is my dog's first bath at home. How do I do it?
Use lukewarm water and a gentle dog shampoo. Brush his coat first to remove tangles.
He hates water.
Then go slowly. Let him stand in the bath area with a treat, talk calmly and wet him a little at a time. Avoid his ears and eyes.
A neighbour's cat visits our house every day and sits on our porch.
That's sweet. Cats like quiet, safe places. Does she look healthy?
Yes, she's fluffy and has a collar.
Then she likely has a home. You can enjoy her visits, but let her owner know she comes here in case they worry.
Can I give her milk?
Water is the safest option. Many cats can't digest milk well, and her owner might have a feeding plan for her.
Okay, I'll put out a bowl of water.
That's kind. Also ask the owner what she may eat, so you don't upset her tummy.
I'll write to them with a note.
Good idea. A friendly note builds trust and keeps the cat safe.
I want to feed the birds on our terrace every morning. Is it a good idea?
Yes, it's lovely to watch them. Put out clean water and a small amount of grains, like millet or rice, in a shallow dish.
Won't it attract pigeons and make a mess?
Maybe, if there's a lot of food. Offer only small amounts and clean the area regularly. Water is the most valuable thing, especially in summer.
What if the cat from next door comes?
Place the dishes in an open, high spot where cats can't surprise the birds, such as on a stand or a railing with clear view.
I'll try the stand then.
Good. Place it where birds can see around, and they'll feel safe to come.
Will they really come every day?
After a week or so, they will learn the time. Keep it regular and be patient.
My friend's going away for the weekend and asked me to look after her rabbit.
That's a big responsibility, but doable. Ask her for clear instructions on food, water and cage cleaning.
What if the rabbit gets out?
Keep the door of the cage secured and any room closed. Rabbits are quick, so have a calm plan, like blocking exits and moving slowly.
Should I let him out to play?
Only if your friend says it's fine and in a safe room. Remove wires and small objects, and supervise all the time.
I'm going to the market and want to bargain, but I feel shy.
It's common to ask for a better price at markets. Do it politely and with a smile. If the seller says no, just say thanks and move on.
What if they get angry?
Most won't. Keep your tone friendly and don't argue. A fair price for both is the goal.
I'm picking a diary for the new year. There are so many designs.
Think about how you will use it. Daily notes need more pages and a firm cover, while a small notebook is easier to carry.
I'll write a little every night.
Then pick one with a page for each day or lined pages. A ribbon marker and a sturdy spine also help.
This one has a lock.
A lock is fun for privacy, but a cover that closes is also fine. Check that the paper is thick enough for pens, so ink doesn't show through.
I'll pick the lock one. It's more fun.
Good. Remember to keep the key in a safe place, so you don't get locked out of your own diary!
My son is growing fast and his uniform is already tight. Should I buy a bigger size?
A slightly bigger size can last longer, but not too big, because loose clothes can look untidy and get in the way.
The school only gives us one shop for it.
Then check if the shop allows exchanges if the size is wrong. Ask about stitching allowances, too, so that hems can be let down as he grows.
Should I buy two sets?
Two sets are practical, so one can be washed while he wears the other. Mark each piece with his name.
Good. I'll take him to try them on.
That's the best way to get a good fit. Let him move around in them to make sure they are comfortable.
Thanks, I'll do that.
Check the seams and buttons before leaving the shop, so you can exchange them immediately if needed.
I want to buy a present for my grandparents' anniversary. They have everything.
People who have everything often appreciate something personal. Is there a memory you share with them?
I love making them laugh by dancing.
Then a handwritten card with a promise of a special dance, plus a small framed photo of all of you, would delight them.
A dance would be fun. They'd record it for sure.
It can become their favourite memory. Ask them about their favourite old song and dance to it.
A friend is fasting during Navratri and I'd like to cook her something she can eat. What would be good?
That's thoughtful. Ask her which foods her family follows, because customs differ. Many people eat sabudana khichdi, kuttu rotis or potato dishes with rock salt.
Does she mind if I cook for her?
Most people appreciate it when a friend cares. Ask her gently and let her guide you with ingredients and utensils.
I'll ask tomorrow.
Good. Make sure to use clean utensils, as she may follow specific rules for her fast.
Diwali cleaning has started and my mom wants me to clean my whole room. I have so much stuff.
It's a big job, but it can feel good when you finish. Start with one corner or one shelf at a time.
Where do I put everything?
Make piles: things to keep, things to give away and things to throw out. Leave the keep pile for last, and put it back neatly.
I found old toys and books.
Those are great to donate. Many schools or community centres take books and toys that are still in good shape.
Good idea. My cousins might like them too.
Then you can give them directly. Check with their parents first, so that they have space.
I'll do that. It feels better now.
Good. Light a small diya in your clean room, and it will feel extra festive.
Our building is going carolling for Christmas. I'm not a good singer.
Carolling is about joy and togetherness, not perfect voices. In a group, you won't stand out.
But I might sing off-key.
Stand near someone who sings well and follow them. A small mistake disappears in the group sound, and people only remember the warm feeling.
I want to make Eid cards for my friends. Any ideas?
A simple card with a crescent moon and stars cut from gold paper looks pretty. Fold coloured card in half and glue the shapes on the front.
What should I write inside?
'Eid Mubarak! Wishing you joy, good food and time with family.' Then add each friend's name.
Can I make them funny?
Yes, if the friend enjoys humour. You could add a small joke about all the sweets you plan to eat.
I'll make one for my teacher too.
That'll be a lovely surprise. Keep hers simple and warm, with thanks for her help during the year.
I have a campus placement talk tomorrow and I'm so nervous.
Nerves are normal. The talk is mostly to give information. Is it a presentation or an interview?
Just a talk by a company.
Then you only need to listen and take notes. You can prepare two questions, such as what skills they look for in new joiners.
A few classmates and I want to share notes for the semester. How do we make it work?
Share a folder where each person uploads their notes for one subject, so the work is divided.
What if someone doesn't upload?
Agree on a deadline each week and remind each other kindly. If someone keeps missing it, talk privately, or divide subjects differently.
What about quality? Some people write messy notes.
Suggest a simple format: date, topic, key points and examples. Check the notes once a week and fix anything unclear.
Great, I'll propose it tomorrow.
Good idea. Start small with two subjects, and add more if it works.
I'm in a study group with five people, and the sessions turn into gossip. How do I fix it?
That's a common problem. Suggest a clear plan before each session, like 'We'll cover chapter four first.' Set a timer.
Won't that sound bossy?
Not if you phrase it as a suggestion, like 'Shall we cover this first and then take a break?' Most people agree that they should get work done.
What if they ignore me?
You can meet with just the one or two classmates who like to focus, and join the big group for fun. It's fine to want to study well.
I'll try the timer idea first.
Good. Keep the breaks short, so the gossip doesn't take over.
Let's hope it works!
Give it two or three sessions. If it works, others will follow.
Typing quickly is my goal. I only use two fingers.
That's very common. Learning to touch type, using all ten fingers, can double your speed. It takes a little practice.
Do I have to look at the keys?
At first you will, but try to use your fingers' memory by keeping them on the home row, which is the middle row of letters. Look at the screen, not the keyboard.
How long will it take?
With fifteen minutes of practice a day, many people notice improvement in two to three weeks. Start slowly and focus on accuracy first.
Are there free lessons online?
Yes, many websites offer free typing lessons and games. Choose one that gives a short daily lesson.
I'll try one tonight.
Good. Sit upright and keep your wrists relaxed, so your hands don't get tired.
I need to email my professor about missing a class. How do I start?
Keep it short and polite. Start with a greeting, state your name and class, explain briefly why you missed it and ask how to catch up.
Could you show me an example?
For example: 'Dear Professor Rao, I'm Meera from your Tuesday class. I missed today's lecture because I was unwell. Could you tell me how I can catch up on the material? Thank you, Meera.'
Should I attach a note?
Only if your college asks for one. You can mention that you can bring it, if needed.
Okay, I'll write it now.
Good. Check the subject line, and read the email once before you send it.
Thanks. It feels easier now.
It does get easier after the first one. Clear and polite is all it takes.
A stranger messaged me in a game chat and wants to be friends.
Be careful with people you only know online. It's fine to chat about the game, but don't share personal details like your school, address or photos.
He seems nice.
People can seem nice and still not be who they say. Keep talking only in the game, and tell a parent or older sibling.
What if he asks for my number?
Say no. A real friend will respect that. If he keeps asking, block him and tell a trusted adult.
I'm trying to set up a daily practice routine for singing. Where do I start?
Pick a fixed time, like the morning or just after school. Begin with five minutes of gentle humming, then sing a scale, then a song.
How long should it be?
Fifteen to twenty minutes a day is enough for beginners. Regular practice is better than one long session.
I have to sing on stage next week and I'm terrified.
It's normal to be afraid. Which song are you singing?
A popular film song.
Choose the part you know best, and practise the whole song until you can sing it without looking at the words.
What if I forget the lyrics?
Keep humming or repeat the line you remember, and join in at the next line. The audience may not notice, because they listen to the tune.
I'm thinking of joining the college choir. I've never sung in a group.
Choirs are welcoming to beginners, and singing together is a joy. They usually have a short try-out to find your voice range.
What if I'm not good enough?
Choirs value people who can listen and blend in as much as strong voices. Try the audition. If you are not selected, you can ask for feedback.
What do I need to prepare?
A short song you know well. Choose something that suits your voice, so it's comfortable to sing.
Will it be a big commitment?
Usually it means one or two rehearsals a week, so check the timetable first. Make sure it fits with your classes.
Okay. I'll go to find out.
Good. Ask them questions about the rehearsal schedule, upcoming concerts and how new members join.
It's so humid today that everything feels sticky and I can't focus.
That's tough. Humid air makes sweat evaporate slowly, so you feel hotter and stickier. Fans and cool water help.
I'm trying to study but can't sit still.
Take your books to the coolest room in the house, wear light cotton clothes and take a short break every half hour to rinse your face.
Sports day is tomorrow and the forecast says rain. We've been practising for weeks.
That's disappointing. Schools often have a backup plan, like moving events to another day or indoors. Has your teacher said anything?
Not yet.
Then wait for the announcement tomorrow morning. Meanwhile, keep your sports kit ready and check with your teacher.
What if it gets postponed?
Then you have more time to practise, and the event will still be there. Your work isn't wasted.
Okay, that makes me feel a bit better.
Good. Keep your kit ready, and use the extra days to rest your legs and fix anything you want to polish.
I like walking in the morning, but winter mornings are so foggy.
Fog makes it hard to see and be seen, so choose a safe route. Walk on footpaths, or in a park if one is nearby.
I wear dark clothes usually.
Switch to brighter colours or add a reflective strip. It helps drivers see you from a distance.
Should I wait until the fog clears?
That's a good option. Mid-morning is usually clearer. If you walk early, take a friend and stay on familiar paths.
My manager asked me to present our project to the whole department. I've never spoken to so many people.
That's a good sign that he trusts you. Prepare a short outline with three main points, and practise aloud.
What if people ask difficult questions?
It's fine to say, 'That's a good question. I'll check and get back to you.' Honesty is better than guessing.
A coworker I really liked is leaving the company. Everyone wants to do something for her.
A farewell is a kind gesture. What does she like?
She loves chocolate and travelling.
Then you could give a small box of chocolates and a card from the whole team. A travel journal would be a nice, personal gift too.
We could also have a team lunch.
Yes, a team lunch lets everyone say goodbye together. Pick a day and place that suits most people and invite her.
Should I make a speech?
A short one is enough. Mention one thing she did well and thank her for her support. Keep it warm and simple.
I'm a bit emotional already.
That's natural. Being sincere matters more than being perfect, and she will probably be touched.
I planted some bean seeds last week and they've started sprouting!
That is great news. Seeing the first green shoot is exciting. Where did you plant them?
In a pot on the window.
A sunny window is perfect for beans. Water them lightly when the top soil is dry, and give them a stick or string to climb as they grow.
How fast will they grow?
Beans grow quickly, often a few centimetres a week. In a month or two you may see flowers and later pods.
There were so many butterflies in our garden today. Why are they here now?
Butterflies come out when the weather is warm and flowers are in bloom, because flowers give them nectar to drink.
They seem to like the yellow flowers.
Many butterflies are attracted to bright colours, and yellow and orange are popular. If you plant more flowers like these, more butterflies will visit.
There's a surprise coming for my birthday tomorrow, I can tell, and I'm too excited to sleep.
What fun. Is it okay to guess what it might be?
I think it's a trip to the zoo.
That would be a great one. Try not to ask your family too many questions. Let them enjoy planning it.
It's so hard to wait.
Do something calm tonight, like reading or a small drawing. A warm drink and an early bedtime will make tomorrow come faster.
Okay, I'll try that.
Enjoy the surprise tomorrow, whatever it is.
I'm feeling grateful today, and I'm not sure why. Everything is just fine.
That's a nice feeling, and ordinary good days deserve to be noticed. It's good that you paused to feel it.
I want to do something with this feeling.
You could write a thank-you note to someone who helped you, or note three good things from today in your diary. It makes the feeling last.
I'll thank my mother. She's done a lot for me.
She'll be happy to hear it. Tell her one specific thing she did, so that it feels real.
I think I'll cook dinner tomorrow too.
That's a thoughtful gift. Plan something simple that you can cook well, and let her relax.
I'm smiling just thinking about it.
Hold on to that. Gratitude is something to practise, and it grows when you do.
I tried pottery at a workshop today and my pot collapsed. It was so funny.
That's a very common first experience. Clay needs even pressure and a steady hand. Did you enjoy it?
Yes! I want to try again.
Then do. The second pot will likely be better, because your hands now know how the clay feels. Keep the walls even and don't make them too thin.
I've started playing chess online but I lose every game.
That's normal at the start. Beginners learn a lot from losses. Do you know the basics, such as how pieces move?
Yes, but I forget to protect my pieces.
That's a very common mistake. Before each move, ask yourself, 'What is my opponent threatening?' It takes a few seconds and saves many pieces.
Is there a way to practise?
Yes, you can try short puzzles, which show a position and ask for the best move. They train you to spot ideas quickly.
I'll start with puzzles.
Good. After each game, look at where you made your first big mistake, and try to learn from it.
I have my first group presentation in class tomorrow and I don't know if I should make slides.
Slides can help, but they aren't compulsory. What is the topic?
The water cycle. We're a team of four.
Then a few simple slides with pictures of rain, clouds and rivers would help. Keep the text short and each person explains one stage.
Okay, I'll make four slides.
Good, one per person. Practise passing the talk smoothly from one speaker to the next.
My mother wants to learn to use video calls to talk to her sister abroad.
That's lovely. Show her how to open the app, tap on her sister's name and press the video button.
She gets nervous about pressing the wrong thing.
Reassure her that she can't break the phone by tapping. Practise with you in the next room, calling her, so she can learn the steps.
I'd like to learn how to make a basic omelette without breaking it.
A simple omelette is easy once you know the steps. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, heat a little oil in a pan on medium heat and pour them in.
Mine always turns into scrambled eggs.
That happens when you stir it. Let the egg set for a minute, then gently fold it in half with a spatula and cook the other side briefly.
What about the heat?
Medium or low is best. Too high and it browns before it cooks inside, and it will break when you flip it.
My friend borrowed my notes and then said she didn't need them. I feel used.
That can feel odd, especially if you took the time to share. Do you think she meant to upset you?
I don't think so, but it hurt.
Then let her know, in a friendly way: 'I was happy to share my notes, but I felt a bit hurt when you said you didn't need them.' Many people don't realise how they sound.
Long-distance running is hard for me because I get a stitch after a short while.
Many beginners feel that. A slower pace usually helps. Are you breathing evenly?
Probably not. I breathe fast.
Try slowing your pace so you can speak in short sentences, and breathe in steadily through the nose and mouth.
Should I walk in between?
Yes, mixing short runs with walking is a good way to build up. Run for two minutes, walk for one, and repeat.
I'll try that on Sunday.
Good. Don't eat a heavy meal just before running, and drink water before and after.
We're going to visit my uncle in a village for a week, and my city friends say I'll be bored.
Village visits can be wonderful. There is often a slower pace, lots of fresh air and plenty to see.
I don't know what to do all day.
Walk through the fields, help with small farm jobs, watch how the food is grown and cooked, and ask your uncle about his life. You may enjoy it more than you expect.
I can take my sketchbook.
Good idea. Sketch the animals, plants and houses. At the end of the week, you'll have a lovely record of the trip.
I have to bring chart paper to school tomorrow and the stationery shop is already closed.

That's annoying, but you have options. Ask a neighbour or cousin if they have a spare sheet, or check whether your teacher would accept plain sheets joined together. A short note to the teacher helps too.
Joined sheets? Won't that look messy?
Not if you overlap the edges by a finger's width and press a heavy book on them until they dry. Draw your border over the join and it will hardly show.
My grandmother asked me to help her write letters to her old schoolfriends. Her handwriting is shaky now.
What a lovely project. You could write exactly what she says, and she can sign each letter herself. How many friends does she want to write to?
About six. She wants to tell them about our family.
Then make a small list first: each friend's name, address and one memory she wants to mention. It keeps the six letters from sounding the same, and it gives her the fun of remembering.
She also wants to put a pressed flower in one of them.
That's sweet. Let the flower dry fully between book pages, then tape it lightly inside a folded sheet. Keep the envelope flat so it doesn't crumble on the way.
She asked me to read the replies to her when they come.
That could be the best part. Read them slowly and let her comment as you go. You might even keep them together in a small box.
I'll use an old shoebox and let her decorate it.
Lovely. She can paste a few photos on the lid, and you'll have a keepsake of the whole project.
When I meet my friend Anil he spends the whole time telling his own stories. I'd like to share mine too.
It's fair to want a turn. Many people talk a lot when they're excited and don't notice. Have you tried starting with something like, 'Can I tell you what happened to me?'
Not really. I usually just listen.
Then try it once. Pick a short story you like and bring it up early, before the chat gets going. A friendly, direct line is usually enough.
What if he cuts in again?
Smile and say, 'Wait, let me finish this bit.' It's polite, and it gives you your turn back.
I'll try on Saturday. At worst it's a funny conversation.
Exactly. And if it goes well, you'll both know how to share the time from then on.
I bought a bunch of coriander and half of it is already wilting. Can I save it?
Often, yes. Trim the stems, put the bunch in a glass of cold water for twenty minutes and it can perk up. For the rest, chop and use it soon.
How do I keep the next bunch fresh?
Wrap the dry leaves in a paper towel and keep them in a box in the fridge. The towel soaks up extra moisture, which is what makes leaves go slimy.
We're taking a ferry for the first time next week. I get nervous around deep water.
That's very common. Ferries are big and steady, and the crew handles that route every day. Do you know how long the crossing is?
About forty minutes.
That's short. You can stand near the middle of the deck, where the movement is smallest, and look at the horizon instead of the waves.
And what if I still feel scared?
Then breathe slowly, count your breaths, and talk to whoever you're travelling with. Talking about something funny works well. Most people find the nervous feeling fades once the boat starts moving.
Okay. I'll bring a book too.
A book is a nice companion for the crossing. Keep it in your hand bag so it's easy to reach, and have a lovely trip.
I'm the only one in my team who didn't get invited to a lunch plan. I might be overthinking, but it stung.
It's natural to feel that. Before deciding what it means, remember that lunch plans are often arranged quickly and someone may simply have forgotten to message you.
Should I ask them about it?
You could, lightly. Something like, 'Are you all going out for lunch today? I'd love to join.' It's friendly and doesn't blame anyone.
That feels less awkward than I expected.
Yes, and if they say yes, you've solved it in one sentence.
Maybe I missed a message. The invites usually come up in the team chat.
That's quite possible. Scroll back through the chat once. If you find nothing, the line you planned still works, and a missed message is nothing unusual.
Our Ganesh pandal needs someone to announce the evening aarti timings, and they picked me. I've never used a microphone.
What an honour. A microphone is easier than it looks. Hold it a little below your mouth and speak slowly, like you're talking to someone at the back of the room.
What if my voice shakes?
Then it shakes, and nobody will mind. Write the timings on a card, so you only have to read, not remember. A few slow breaths before you start will steady you.
Can I practise somewhere?
Yes. Stand in your hall and read the card aloud to a family member at the other end. If you can be heard there, you'll be fine at the pandal.
The committee says I'll announce on Saturday. What should I wear?
Something comfortable and festive, nothing you'd have to adjust while speaking. A simple kurta or salwar is just right.
Any other tips for the day?
Drink some water beforehand, arrive early to test the microphone and keep your card in your hand. Smile before you start, since it softens your voice.
I joined a badminton class and everyone else already knows how to smash. I only know how to hit the shuttle back.
That's a perfectly good start. A smash comes from timing and a relaxed wrist, and those are learned in class, not before. Your coach will expect beginners.
How long before I can smash?
It varies a lot. Some people manage a weak smash in a few weeks, others take months. Practising clear, high shots first will make the smash easier.
Haha, so my 'hit it back' is actually training.
Exactly. Solid basics are what every good smash is built on.
Do I need special shoes?
Not at first. Comfortable sports shoes with good grip are enough for a beginner. If you stay with the sport, your coach can advise on better ones.
My coach said the same.
Ha, two sources agreeing is a good sign. Enjoy the class.
A snail has been sitting on our wall for two days. Is it stuck?
Probably not. Snails often rest for long stretches, especially when it's dry, and seal themselves to a surface to keep their moisture in.
Should I move it to the garden?
You can. If it has sealed itself, don't pull it, because that could hurt it. Sprinkle a few drops of water near it and it may loosen up on its own by evening.
I want to read a book about space but I'm not good at science. Is that okay?
Yes, plenty of space books are written for ordinary readers, with plain words and lots of pictures. You don't need any science to enjoy them.
How do I pick one that's not too hard?
Read the first page in the shop or library. If you understand most of it and want to turn the page, it's the right level. A book for young readers is nothing to be embarrassed about.
I'll look for one with pictures then.
Nice. Pictures of planets and nebulas make a good starting point, and you can read the parts you like first.
Maybe the library has a section for that.
Many libraries do, often marked for young readers. The librarian can also point you to space books at your level, which saves time.
I woke up sad today and I don't even know why.
That happens to everyone sometimes. A mood can show up without a clear reason. Did you sleep badly or have a long day yesterday?
Slept late, yes.
That could be part of it. Tiredness makes everything feel heavier. Drink some water, get some daylight and have something to eat, and see if it lifts a little.
What if it doesn't?

Then talk to someone you trust, like a parent or a close friend, and tell them what you told me. If it keeps happening for many days, a teacher or counsellor can help too. You don't have to work it out alone.
Okay. I'll tell my mom after school.
That's a kind thing to do for yourself. I hope the afternoon feels lighter.
My parrot says 'hello' to everyone except me. It feels personal.
Ha, parrots do have favourites in what they say. He may simply associate that word with the people who visit. Do you talk to him often?
Mostly I just feed him.
Try giving him a short phrase each time you bring food, such as 'good morning'. Parrots link sounds to moments, so he may start saying it just for you.
How long will that take?
It can take a few weeks of daily repeating, and some birds never pick up words. Either way, regular friendly chatter builds trust.
What phrase should I start with?
Something short and clear, like 'good morning' or his name. Say it in the same cheerful voice every time.
I'll start tomorrow when I fill his bowl.
That's the perfect moment, since he already links you with food. Be patient and keep it fun.
I want to start a small herb corner for cooking, but I've only ever killed money plants.
Herbs like mint and coriander are forgiving, so they're a good start. Even people who say they have no green thumb often manage mint, because it grows eagerly.
What do I need?
A pot with holes at the bottom, soil, seeds or a cutting, and a spot with a few hours of sun. Water when the top of the soil feels dry, not every time you walk past.
Not every time I walk past. That's my problem.
Then it's good you know it. A reminder on a calendar for every second day can keep you from drowning it with kindness.
I set a reminder. Which herb should I try first?
Mint or coriander. Mint is the easiest to keep alive, and coriander gives quick leaves for cooking.
I'll go for mint, since it's hard to kill.
Do keep it in its own pot, though. Mint spreads fast and can crowd out other plants.
Our curtains keep catching on the window latch and tearing a little each time.
That's a simple fix. You can cover the latch with a small piece of soft cloth or tape, or hang the curtains a bit away from the window using a longer rod.
The tear is already small. Can I mend it?
Yes. Turn the curtain inside out, stitch the tear with small even stitches in matching thread, and press it flat. A small patch from the hem can hide a larger one.
I'll try the tape first and see how it goes.
Sensible. It costs nothing and protects the cloth while you decide.
The tape held up, but the curtain still looks tired. Should I just wash it?
Washing can freshen it. Check the label first, because some cloth shrinks. If it says hand wash, use cold water and dry it in the shade.
It's been foggy every morning this week. Why does it happen so often in winter?
Cold nights cool the air close to the ground, and the air can't hold as much water vapour when it's cold. The extra vapour turns into tiny droplets, which we see as fog.
So it's like the cloud has come down?
Pretty much. Fog is a cloud touching the ground. When the sun warms the air, the droplets turn back into vapour and the fog usually clears by late morning.
Our neighbour practises the flute at dawn and I actually enjoy it. Is that weird?
Not at all. Hearing someone practise is often like a free concert. Do you know the tune?
No, but it's calm. It makes my mornings better.
Then you could tell them you like it. Musicians are usually glad to hear that someone enjoys their practice, and it might make their early mornings better too.
My brother's phone screen cracked and he wants to keep using it. Is that safe?
A small crack is often fine for a while, but it can get worse, and sharp edges can scratch fingers. A cover or screen guard can help in the meantime.
He can't afford a repair right now.
Then a clear tape or screen guard over the crack is a decent short-term fix. Ask a repair shop for a price when it's convenient, and he could also ask a family member if there's an old spare phone.
I just realised my timetable has two classes at the same hour on Tuesdays.
That needs sorting out soon. Check the timetable again to see if one is for a different batch. If it's a real clash, speak to your class coordinator.
It's real. I double-checked.
Then email or visit the coordinator today, say which two classes clash and ask which one you should attend. Many colleges have a standard way of fixing this.
Will I be marked absent from one of them?
Ask that in the same message. Once the coordinator knows about the clash, they can tell you whether it will be recorded, so you aren't guessing.
The coordinator said I can attend one class and get notes for the other. Is that alright?
That sounds sensible. Ask a classmate in the other class to share their notes, and thank them properly.
How should I ask?
Try, 'I have a timetable clash on Tuesdays and will miss your class. Could I borrow your notes after each lecture?' Offer to share yours from the other class in return.
The shopkeeper gave me too much change and I only noticed after I left. The shop is two streets away.
Returning it is the honest thing to do, and it's usually easy. Is the shop still open?
Yes, for another hour.
Then walk back with the extra money, say what happened, and hand it over. Shopkeepers are usually grateful, and it keeps your day free of niggling thoughts.
Okay. I'll go now.
That's a nice thing to do. Safe walk.
Someone left a pile of old furniture on our street corner and it's been there for days.
That would be annoying to walk past. Is there a residents' group or a local office that handles waste in your area?
There's a resident committee.
Then message the committee with the exact spot and, if you can, a photo. They will know who to contact to clear it. It's quicker than asking around the street.
Our teacher wants us to bring something that starts with each letter of our name for a class activity. My name is Kavya.
Fun challenge. For K you could bring a key or a kite. Do you have anything small at home that begins with each of the other letters?
A, V, Y, A. I'm stuck on V and Y.
For V, try a vase, a toy violin or a small vegetable like a vine leaf. For Y, a yo-yo, a ball of yarn or a yellow object works well. The yarn would be easy to carry.
A yellow yo-yo would cover Y twice!
Ha, a very good cheat. Just make sure it fits your class rules.
She said pictures are fine too, so I'll draw a violin if I can't find one.
That works well. A neat drawing with a label shows effort, and you won't have to carry anything fragile.
My dad and I are trying to cook breakfast together every Sunday, but we always argue about what to make.
What a nice habit, and arguing about breakfast is a good problem to have. You could take turns picking the dish.
He always chooses poha.
Then it's fine to ask for your turn. Maybe say, 'This Sunday is my pick, next Sunday is yours.' Keep a list on the fridge so it feels fair, not like a fight.
And if my pick is complicated?
Then he can help, and it will become part of the fun. Start with something simple, like masala toast, and move to bigger things later.
He'd actually love masala toast.
Then you have a plan. Maybe he will pick your idea next time too.
My friend Tara and I like different kinds of movies. She likes horror and I get scared easily.
That's a very ordinary difference. You can still plan fun things together. What kinds of movies do you like?
Comedies and animated ones.
Then take turns: one movie night for her pick, one for yours. For her horror film, you could watch it in the afternoon with the lights on and snacks ready.
Daytime horror, that's a smart idea.
Right? Horror is a lot less frightening at three in the afternoon with a bowl of popcorn.
She picked a film for Saturday. It's about a haunted house.
Then set the stage for comfort. Choose a bright room, keep a blanket nearby and plan something funny for afterwards.
A comedy chaser, I like it.
It balances the evening nicely, and you'll both go to bed relaxed.
I want to make a sandwich for lunch but I only have bread, cheese, tomato and cucumber.
That's enough for a nice one. Layer thin slices of cheese, tomato and cucumber between two slices of bread, and add a pinch of salt on the tomato.
Can I grill it without a toaster?
Yes, use a flat pan on low heat. If you have a drop of oil or butter, put it on the pan; if not, a dry non-stick pan works. Press the sandwich with a plate, and flip it when the underside is golden.
It worked! Though the cheese leaked out.
That's normal. Next time, keep the cheese a little away from the edges, and the crispy burnt bits will taste great anyway.
My family is going to visit a fort next weekend. What can I do to enjoy it more than the last time we went somewhere historical?
A few small things help a lot. Read a short bit about the fort before you go, so you have a story in mind, and bring a notebook for sketches or questions. What didn't you enjoy last time?
It was just walking and reading boards.
Then give yourself a game. Look for one hidden detail in each room, such as carvings, small windows or old stairs. Ask a guide a few questions if there is one.
That sounds more fun than reading boards.
It usually is. You could also take photos of your favourite spots and make a small album afterwards.
My brother wants to go to the highest point of the fort. Should we?
If the climb is open and looks safe, it's usually the best view. Check the steps and rails, wear shoes with grip and go slowly.
Okay. We'll take water too.
Smart. Carry it in a bag with a strap, so your hands are free for the rails.
My supervisor praised my work today, and I just said 'thanks' and froze. I wish I'd said more.
'Thanks' is a perfectly good response. Praise can catch us off guard. You could add a line later, such as, 'I'm glad it helped the team.'
Is it okay to say that the next day?
Yes. A short follow-up is thoughtful, and it shows you appreciated the comment.
Okay, I'll say it tomorrow morning.
That's a nice plan. Keep it to one warm sentence and you're done.
We're making diyas at home from clay this Diwali. I've never done it.
That sounds like a lovely activity. Shape a small ball of clay, press your thumb into the centre, then pinch one side so the wick can rest there.
How long should they dry?
Dry them in the shade for a day or two, turning them sometimes. Direct strong sun can crack the clay. A gentle coat of paint after drying makes them look festive.
Mine are a bit uneven.
Uneven diyas look handmade, which is part of the charm. Make a few extra, so you can pick the best ones for the front.
My school wants me to run in a relay race, but I'm afraid of dropping the baton.
That's a very common worry, and even good runners practise passing a lot. Hold the baton firmly and pass it with a clear 'now' signal to the next runner.
Where do I practise?
Any open space works. Ask a friend to stand ahead, jog at a steady pace and practise the handover many times, first slowly, then faster. Your sports teacher can also show you the right way.
Will we really use the word 'now'?
Many teams do, since it keeps the pass clear. Agree on the signal with your team before the race.
I want to know why leaves are green, because my little cousin asked and I couldn't answer.
Leaves are green because they contain a pigment called chlorophyll, which absorbs red and blue light to make food for the plant and reflects green light back to our eyes.
Chlorophyll. How do I explain that to a child?
Say that leaves are like little kitchens. They use sunlight to make food, and the tool they use is a green substance that reflects green light.
Kitchens! She'll like that.
Great. You could even take her on a leaf hunt and compare greens afterwards.
Her next question was why leaves turn yellow in autumn.
The tree stops making chlorophyll, so the green fades. That lets the yellow and orange colours, which were there all along, show through.
So the yellow was always inside?
Yes, hidden under the green. It's a nice thing to point out on your leaf hunt.
I started a book in the series my friend loves and I don't know if I should read the first book first.
Usually it's best to start with the first book, because the story builds on earlier events and characters. Which book are you on now?
Book three. Everyone has been talking about it.
You could keep reading book three, and notice if you feel lost. If you do, read a short summary of the first two online or from your friend, and then fill in the missing parts later.
My friend can tell me the story of the first two. That would save time.
That's a friendly shortcut. Just remember that hearing it from your friend may spoil surprises.
What if I read book three first and go back to book one later?
You can, but you may learn big surprises from book three that change how book one feels. If that doesn't bother you, the choice is yours.
I can't stop smiling today because my cousin I haven't seen in two years is coming tonight.
That's wonderful to hear. Two years is a long time. Have you made any plans?
We'll stay up late and talk. I've made a list of everything I want to tell her.
A list sounds like a good idea. You will have so much to catch up on. Keep your phone away for a while, so the evening is only yours and hers.
My dog hides under the bed every time there are firecrackers outside. How do I help him?
Dogs find loud noises scary. Let him stay in his hiding place if he feels safe there, and sit close by, speaking calmly. Don't force him out.
Should I close the windows?
Yes, closing windows and curtains and playing soft music or a fan can reduce the noise. A quiet inner room is best.
He seems calmer with me next to him.
Then keep doing that. If he is very upset every time, ask your vet for advice for the next festival season.
Thinking of starting a stamp collection. Where do stamps even come from?
You can find them on old letters and parcels from family and neighbours. Ask people to save envelopes for you, and cut stamps out with a small border of paper.
How do I remove the paper from the stamp?
Soak the stamp in lukewarm water for a few minutes until the paper slips off, then dry it flat on a clean cloth. Handle it by the edges so it doesn't tear.
Do I keep them in a notebook?
A small album with clear pockets or paper corners is better than glue, which would damage the stamps. Write the country and year beside each one if you can find it.
How do I find stamps from other countries?
Ask relatives or friends who get foreign mail to save them, or swap with other collectors. A school or hobby club may have a swap day.
A swap day would be perfect.
Then ask your teacher if the school could host one. Even a small table of collectors helps.
My room feels dark even in the daytime, and I'd like to brighten it without spending much.
Light-coloured curtains that let sunlight through make a big difference. Do you have a window that faces the sun?
Yes, but the curtain is heavy and dark.
Try a thin, light curtain, or just tie the heavy one back during the day. Keep the area near the window free of tall furniture. A mirror on the wall opposite the window also bounces light around.
They say it'll be very windy tonight. What should I do about my balcony plants?
Move the small pots indoors or to a sheltered corner, and tie taller plants to a support. Keep anything light, like pot saucers, away from the edge so it can't blow off.
What about the big pot I can't lift?
Place it against a wall, away from the railing, and tuck smaller pots around it. If it's tall, you can tie it loosely to the railing with a soft cloth strip.
Great, I'll do that after dinner.
Do it before it gets dark, so you can see what you're doing.
The wind calmed down by morning and everything is still in place.
Glad your plants made it. Put the pots back in their usual spots and water any that look dry, since wind dries soil faster than you'd expect.
I can play three songs on the keyboard. How do I get better without a teacher?
Pick one song and practise it slowly in small pieces, rather than playing it through. Fix the tricky bars until they feel easy, then join the pieces.
How long should I practise?
Short and regular beats long and rare. Twenty minutes a day is better than two hours once a week.
Okay, and what should I learn after these songs?
Try one in a different style, so you stretch your fingers in new ways. You can also learn some simple scales, which help every song you play.
My little sister keeps pressing buttons on my laptop while I'm working. I lost an hour's work yesterday.
That's frustrating. Is there a setting where the laptop saves your work automatically?
Not sure. I use a simple text editor.

Most editors have an autosave option, or you can press the save shortcut every few minutes. For the future, you could give your sister a different activity, like a drawing app of her own, when you work.
She'd love her own drawing time.
Then fix a time each day for it. She'll be happier, and your laptop will be left alone.
Should I give her a drawing app or just paper?
Either works. Paper is simpler for a small child and doesn't need your laptop, but a simple drawing program with big buttons can be fun too. Keep the sessions short.
Paper, then. Fewer ways to break things.
A wise choice. Give her fat crayons and your laptop will be safe.
I have to read a research paper for class and the first page already confuses me.
That's normal. Papers are written for specialists, so don't read them like a story. Start with the title, the summary at the top and the conclusion.
Then what?
Go back and read the introduction, then the main sections slowly. Underline words you don't know and look them up after you finish each page. Ask your teacher whether a simpler reading is available.
Time for a new water bottle, but I can't decide between steel and plastic.
Both work. Steel lasts longer and doesn't hold smells, while plastic is lighter and cheaper. How do you carry it?
In my school bag, and I walk a lot.
Then a light plastic one might be easier on your shoulders. If you pick steel, choose a small size, so it isn't heavy. Check that the lid closes tightly to protect your books.
I'll check the lid first, I think.
Sure. Shake it upside down over a sink before you pay, in case the lid leaks. If it does, pick another one.
Our colony's water tank is cleaned only once a year and some neighbours want it done more often.
That's a reasonable thing to raise. Do you know who looks after it?
The secretary. He says it costs a lot.

You could ask him politely how the cost is shared and whether the neighbours can discuss a schedule together. Something like every six months might be an easy middle point. Raise it at the next meeting, calmly, with the others who agree.
Should I put it in writing?
A short written note is useful, because it can be added to the meeting list. Keep it polite and simple, and mention the reason, which is clean water for everyone.
I keep forgetting small tasks my manager asks for in passing.
That's easy to fix. Write each request down as soon as you hear it, even on a small notebook. Do you have something with you in meetings?
No, I just remember.
Try keeping a pocket notebook or a notes app, and glance at it twice a day. A short list at the start of the day and a check at the end works well.
What if I forget to check?
Then set two reminders on your phone, one in the morning and one before you leave. After a few weeks, it becomes a habit.
I'll buy a notebook tomorrow.
A plain notebook is all you need. Keep it with a pen in the same spot every day, so you can always find it.
I get very sleepy in the last period of the day and can't follow the lesson.
That is common. Does it happen only in that class, or in others too?
Mostly the last one.
Try drinking water at lunch and sitting up straight, and ask if you can note down key points. Making small notes keeps your mind busy. If you stay very sleepy every day, mention it to your parents.
Notes make sense. Should I tell the teacher too?
You can, in a polite way, such as, 'I find it hard to stay alert at this hour. Can I stand for a moment to stretch?' Most teachers will understand.
I'm going on a school trip and I'm supposed to pack in one small bag.
That's a good challenge. Start by writing a list of what you absolutely need, such as clothes for each day, toiletries, a water bottle and any medicines your parents give you.
I think I need three shirts, a jacket and two pairs of trousers.
That's reasonable. Roll the clothes instead of folding them, to save space. Wear the bulkiest items, like the jacket, when you travel.
And my slippers?
Put them in a plastic bag at the bottom of the bag so the dirt stays out. Slip a pair of socks inside them to fill the space.
Great, I'll practise packing tonight.
Practising is smart. Pack the bag, close it and lift it. If it's too heavy to carry comfortably, take something out.
Our neighbours have invited us for their Christmas tea and I don't know what to bring.
A small, simple gift is lovely. Home-baked cookies, a box of sweets or a small plant are all easy choices. Do you know if anyone has food restrictions?
I'm not sure. I think one of them avoids eggs.
Then egg-free options are safest, such as dry fruit or plain biscuits. You could ask your neighbour when you reply to the invitation, so you don't guess.
I'll ask, and bring a small plant otherwise.
A plant is a lovely idea. Add a small card with your best wishes.
I'd like to try yoga but I can't touch my toes.
That doesn't matter. Yoga is about slow movement and breathing, and flexibility improves with time. Start with a beginner class or a gentle online video.
Will it hurt if I can't bend?
You shouldn't push into pain. Move only as far as feels comfortable, and stop if something hurts. If you have any health concerns, check with a doctor before you start.
I saw a bright blue bird on our wire today. It was beautiful.
How lovely. Do you remember anything else about it, such as its size or tail?
It was about the size of a pigeon and had a long tail.
It might be a roller or a similar bird, but I can't say for sure without seeing it. A local bird guide or a bird-watching group could help you identify it.
I'll look at the pictures in a bird book at the library.
A good plan. Note the date and place in a notebook too, so you can see if it visits again.
My friend Meera hums loudly during our study sessions. I like her, but I can't concentrate.

That sounds distracting, and it's okay to say so kindly. She may not even realise. You could try, 'I can't focus when there's humming. Could we keep it quiet for thirty minutes and then have a song break?'
A song break is a great idea. She'll like that.
Then she has something to look forward to. Set a phone alarm for both parts so it stays fair.
My mom says rice should be soaked before cooking but I never do. Does it matter?
It can help. Soaked rice cooks faster and more evenly, and the grains often turn out fluffier. Twenty to thirty minutes is usually enough.
And if I forget?
Then cook it as usual with a little extra water and more time. Rinse it well first, so it doesn't turn sticky.
My parents want a family photo for the wall, and everyone has a different idea about where and what to wear.
A fun problem to have. A family photo works best when the plan is simple. What does each person want?
Dad wants it at home, Mom wants a studio, and my brother wants matching T-shirts.

Each idea has a point. Home is relaxed and free, a studio gives proper lighting, and matching clothes look tidy. You could combine them: take it at home in the best-lit spot, with everyone in one or two colours.
Matching colours instead of the same shirt?
Yes. If everyone wears blue or white, the photo looks planned but nobody feels like they're in a uniform.
Where in the house is the best light?
Usually near a big window in the morning or late afternoon. Stand the group so the light falls on your faces, not behind you.
I'll tell them the plan tonight. Mom will probably love the colours idea.
I hope so. Offer it as a suggestion and let them add their own touches, so everyone feels heard.
There's a new word on almost every page of my book. I look up each one and it's taking forever.
That slows the reading and spoils the story. Try guessing from the sentence first. Mark the words that seem important and look up only those after you finish the chapter.
What if I guess wrong?
You'll find out when you look it up, and a wrong guess is a good way to remember the word. Often you don't need the exact meaning to follow the story.
How many words should I look up per chapter?
Five or six is plenty. Pick the ones that appear more than once, since they're likely to be useful.
Should I write them down?
Yes, in a small notebook, with the meaning and the sentence where you found it. A few minutes of review each week helps them stick.
That feels doable. I might even enjoy it.
You probably will, once the reading flows. At the end of the month, look through your notebook and see how many words you know now.
Our school magazine is asking for submissions and I'd like to send a poem, but I'm not sure it's good enough.
Sending it is already brave. Magazines like to see work from students at every level. What is the poem about?
It's about the sound of rain on our tin roof.
That's a vivid subject. Poems about small, real sounds often work well. Read it aloud once and cut any line that doesn't help the picture.
How long should it be?
Check the magazine's guidelines first. If there's no limit, keep it to one page, so every line has to earn its place.
I'll ask the editor teacher tomorrow.
That's the best way to be sure. Bring a neat copy with your name and class on it.
Thanks. If it doesn't get picked I'll just send another one next time.
A lovely attitude. Many writers send work several times before it gets in, so keep writing.
My cousin is staying with us this week and she snores. I haven't slept well.
That sounds tiring. Is there a quiet corner or another room where you could sleep?
We only have one room, so we share.
Then try a few simple things: earplugs or soft music through headphones, and a short nap in the afternoon if you can. You could also ask her to sleep on her side, which sometimes lessens the sound.
Won't she be offended if I ask?
Say it kindly and lightly, like, 'I'm having trouble sleeping. Could you try turning on your side tonight?' Most people take a gentle request well.
She laughed and said she'd try. What can I do tonight in case it still happens?
Keep earplugs or soft sounds through headphones nearby. A pillow over one ear also helps, and a short afternoon nap makes up for lost sleep.
Soft rain sounds. That fits the monsoon!
Ha, that's cosy. Set a timer so it switches off after an hour.
I accidentally called my friend by her sister's name in front of everyone. She looked hurt.
That would sting for her and for you. The best step is a quick, sincere apology. Have you spoken to her yet?
No, I froze.
Find a quiet moment and say, 'I'm sorry I mixed up the names. I know that's not nice to hear.' Keep it short, so it doesn't turn into a long explanation.
What if she's still upset?
Give her space and let her know you care. People often feel better after a day, once they see you were not careless on purpose.
She just replied 'okay' and nothing else.
That's a small sign she's heard you, even if she's still a bit hurt. Let her come to you when she's ready.
Should I send her something funny?
Wait a day. A joke too soon can look like you're not taking it seriously. A warm, normal chat tomorrow will do more.
I put too much salt in the dal and now it's almost inedible.
Don't throw it out yet. You can stretch the dal with more water and cooked dal or lentils, so the salt spreads over a bigger pot.
I don't have more dal, just rice.
Then serve it over a larger portion of plain rice, which soaks up the salty flavour. A squeeze of lemon and a spoon of curd on the side also softens it.
Curd, that's a good idea. I have some.
Great. Taste a small spoon first and add curd bit by bit. Next time, add the salt a little at a time and taste as you go.
It's still a bit salty after the curd. Any last trick?
Add more plain rice to the plate and serve a cooling salad of cucumber and onion on the side. Any leftover dal can become a flavour base, mixed with a fresh pot next time.
I'm going to a hill station and my aunt says I'll get car sick on the curvy road.
That's a common worry on winding roads. Which seat do you usually sit in?
Usually the back.
Try the front seat if you can, and look at the road ahead rather than at your phone or a book. Fresh air from an open window also helps.
What if it happens anyway?
Ask the driver to stop for a short break, step out for fresh air and sip some water. It's all right to ask, because everyone prefers a short pause to a messy one.
Okay. I'll sit in front and keep a bag handy just in case.
Sensible, and a few plain biscuits can calm your stomach. Enjoy the view when you get there.
We're getting a new person on our team on Monday and I've been asked to show her around.
That's a nice responsibility. What do you think she'll want to know first?
Probably where things are and who does what.
Then plan a short walk: show her the desks, the printer, the pantry and where to find the rest rooms, then introduce her to a few people with a line about each person's role.
What if I don't know the answer to her question?
Say, 'I'm not sure, but let's find out.' Then ask a colleague together. It shows her how the team helps each other.
She asked where she should sit at lunch. Should I introduce her to our lunch group?
Yes, it's welcoming. Say, 'We usually eat together at one. Would you like to join us?' She can say no, and you've still been kind.
I'll invite her. She seemed nervous.
That helps more than you'd think. A friendly face on the first day is one of the best things you can offer.
We're hosting a small Eid get-together for neighbours this year and I want to decorate.
How lovely. Do you have a theme or colours in mind?
Green and white, maybe with fairy lights.
That sounds elegant. Hang the lights along the window or door, use a white tablecloth with green cushions or napkins, and put some flowers in the centre.
I only have a few lights.
Concentrate them in one spot, like around the entrance or a table. A small group of lights looks cosy, and the rest of the space can stay simple.
I'll do the entrance. That will be the first thing guests see.
Exactly, a warm welcome sets the mood for the whole evening.
I want to learn to cycle with no hands, like my friend does, but I'm scared of falling.
It takes balance and practice, so go step by step. Are you comfortable cycling on a flat, empty road?
Yes, but only with both hands on the bars.
Then I'd suggest practising first on an open ground without traffic. Ride slowly and lift one hand for a second, then put it back. Do this a few times before trying both.
Should I wear a helmet?
Yes, always for tricks like this, and keep to a flat, empty area. If you can, have a friend nearby.
There's a banyan tree near our school with long roots hanging down. Why does it grow like that?
Those are called aerial roots. They grow from the branches down toward the soil, and when they reach it they thicken into extra trunks that support the heavy branches.
So the tree makes its own pillars?
Yes, that's a good way to put it. A single banyan can spread over a huge area this way, which is why some seem like small forests.
I'm trying to read a few pages every night, but I fall asleep in two minutes.
That says you're tired, not that the book is bad. Is it a book you're excited about?
It's okay. I picked it because everyone said it was famous.
Then perhaps swap it for one you really want to read. A story you enjoy keeps you awake longer, and you can try the famous one another time.
Is that allowed?
Absolutely. Reading is for you, not for anyone else's list. Pick something short and fun to get the habit going.
Which kind of book keeps me awake, though?
Short chapters and a fast plot help. Mysteries and adventures work well, since each chapter ends with a reason to turn the page.
I like mysteries. I'll find a short one.
Nice pick. Read sitting in a chair instead of lying down, and you'll last longer.
Everyone at the party was laughing and I felt like I didn't fit in.
That's an uncomfortable feeling, and a lot of people have it at gatherings. Did you talk to anyone?
Only one person. Then I stood at the edge.
Sometimes it's easier to join a smaller group or help with something, like handing out snacks. That gives you a reason to talk and takes the pressure off.
Next time I'll try that.
I think you'll do fine. Also remember that others may be feeling just as unsure, even when they look relaxed.
That's comforting.
I'm glad. You noticed how you felt, and that's a good step towards handling it.
Our goldfish seems to be swimming at the top of the tank and gulping at the water. Is it hungry?
It might not be hunger. Gulping at the surface can mean the water has too little oxygen. When was the water last changed?
About three weeks ago.
A partial water change may help, using water that has been left to stand for a day. Don't change all of it at once.
Should I ask someone about this?
Yes, a pet shop or a vet who treats fish can check the tank properly. In the meantime, don't overfeed, because extra food dirties the water.
I'd love to learn how to juggle with three balls.
Fun skill. Start with one ball: toss it from hand to hand in an arc at about eye height. Once that feels easy, move to two.
I can't even do two without dropping one.
That's a normal stage. With two balls, throw one, and when it reaches the top, throw the second. Count 'one, two' in your head to find the rhythm.
Do I need real juggling balls?
No, soft things like rolled-up socks work fine and don't roll away. Practise over a bed, so you aren't bending to pick up balls each time.
Rolled-up socks, I have plenty of those.
Perfect. Practise for ten minutes a day, and you'll see improvement within a week or two.
Our window has a squeaky latch that wakes me up every time the wind blows.
A tiny drop of oil on the hinge or latch usually fixes that. Do you have cooking oil or any light oil?
We have coconut oil.
That's fine in a pinch. Put a drop on a cotton bud, rub it on the latch and move the latch back and forth to spread it. Wipe off any extra so it doesn't drip.
What if the squeak is from the frame?
Then ask a family member to look at it with you. A small bit of cloth wedged in the gap can stop the rattle in the meantime.
The oil worked. Now the door hinge creaks too.
Same trick. One drop of oil on the hinge pin, then open and close the door a few times. Wipe off any extra.
I'm becoming the oil person of the house.
Ha, it's a useful title. Keep the bottle in one place so people know who to ask.
It's been drizzling for three days and my laundry won't dry.
That's a monsoon classic. Do you have a fan or a spot with some airflow?
There's a fan in the hall.
Hang the clothes in the hall with the fan on low, leaving space between each piece so air moves through them. Wring them out well after washing, because it saves a lot of drying time.
Can I iron them dry?
A light ironing can finish the job once clothes are nearly dry, which also takes out the damp smell. Don't iron soaking clothes, as it wastes time and can damage them.
Thanks. I'll try that.
Hope the sun peeks out soon. If a damp smell lingers, a splash of vinegar in the last rinse can help.
My brother wants to learn drums but we live in a flat and the neighbours are close.
That needs a bit of planning. A practice pad, which is a rubber surface that makes much less sound, is a common choice for beginners.
Is it enough to learn on?
It's very good for learning grip and rhythm. When he's ready for a full kit, you can look into a practice room or music school nearby.
Do you think we should tell the neighbours first?
It's polite to tell them and fix some hours, such as late afternoon. Neighbours often appreciate being asked first.
Good point. I'll mention it to our neighbour tomorrow.
That's a thoughtful step. A short chat now can prevent many problems later.
My phone keeps asking me to update and I keep saying 'later'. Is that a problem?
Updates often fix bugs and security gaps, so it's better not to ignore them for too long. What stops you from updating?
I'm scared it will delete my photos.
That's a fair worry. Before updating, back up your photos to another place, such as a computer or cloud storage. After that, the update is rarely a risk.
How do I back them up?
You can connect the phone to a computer and copy the photos over, or use the backup option in settings. If you're unsure, ask a family member to sit with you the first time.
I'm supposed to submit an assignment tomorrow and I just discovered my printer has no ink.
That's stressful. Is there a copy shop near your college or home?
Yes, near the college gate. It opens at nine.
Then save the file on a pen drive or email it to yourself tonight, and print it there before class. Check your first class time, so you leave early enough.
What if the shop has a queue?
Go a bit before opening and get your pages printed first. Also check whether your teacher accepts soft copies, as a backup.
I printed it, but now the pages are out of order.
Check the page numbers and rearrange before stapling. If they aren't numbered, match the last line of each page to the first line of the next.
Fixed. It's two minutes to class.
Then walk quickly and go in quietly. Your work is ready, and that's what counts.
I'd like to get a gift for my friend who moved to a cold city. She likes warm things.
A cosy gift is a lovely thought. Do you know her taste, like colours or what she already owns?
She loves purple and she's always cold.
A soft purple scarf or a pair of warm socks would suit her. They're easy to post and she can use them every day.
A scarf, definitely.
A good pick. Add a small handwritten note, so she feels the warmth even when she's far away.
I'll write one tonight.
She'll treasure it.
Our neighbourhood children never play outside anymore. I'd like to start a weekend games hour.
That's a lovely idea. Where would you hold it?
In the small park near our lane.
Then ask a few parents first, and pick a fixed time, such as Sunday at five. Start with simple games like tag, kho-kho or a skipping rope.
What if only two kids turn up?
