My teacher says I should wear better shoes.
Mentioning the shoes to your parents is a good idea too. I can't tell what is causing the knee pain, so please let a doctor check it.
I'll tell my parents tonight and ask them to check.
That's the right plan. Tell them exactly where it hurts and when it happens, and follow the doctor's advice.
I'm going to a cold hill station and don't own a heavy coat.
Layers are a good plan for the cold. Do you have sweaters and warm socks?
Two sweaters and woolly socks.
Wear a thin layer, then a sweater, then something warm and windproof on top, if you have it. A cap or scarf keeps your head and neck warm. Gloves help too if you have them.
I'll borrow a scarf from my cousin. Thanks!
Great. You'll be warm and comfortable, and you'll enjoy the views.
We're planning a Holi get-together for our building, and some neighbours are worried about colours.
Good to hear that you're thinking of everyone. What are they worried about?
Stains on walls and kids' eyes.
You could choose an open area, use natural or skin-safe colours and put old cloth on walls. Tell children to keep colours away from eyes and faces.
Good, I'll make a list of rules and tell the others at the meeting.
That should keep the day cheerful for everyone. Put the rules on a notice board too, so late arrivals see them.
I watched ants carry a dead beetle across the path. How can they lift something so big?
Ants are very strong for their size, and they work together. Many carry the load as a team.
How do they decide where to go?
They follow scent trails and signals from other ants. If one path is blocked, they try another way.
That's fascinating. I'll watch them again tomorrow.
Good plan. Bring a notebook, and see whether you can spot which direction the ants carry things.
I'd like a phone for my birthday, but my parents say I'm too young.
Parents often have reasons about safety and time. Have they told you their main worry?
They think I'd play games all day.
You could suggest a plan, such as limits on hours, homework first and the phone kept outside the bedroom at night. Showing that you can be responsible may help.
That seems fair. I'll show them the plan this weekend.
Good plan. Offering a trial period, like two weeks, shows you are serious and gives them a chance to see how it goes.
I want to read more but I get distracted by my phone.
That's a common problem. Where do you usually read?
On my bed, with my phone nearby.
Try placing the phone in another room, and set a timer for twenty minutes of reading. Short sessions are easier to keep up.
I'll try the timer tonight. Hopefully I won't peek at the phone.
A timer is a gentle trick. If your phone does buzz in the other room, remember it will still be there when your twenty minutes are over.
Our neighbour's tree drops leaves in our yard every day.
That's a bit of a chore. Do you get on well with your neighbour?
Yes, they're friendly.
Then mention it kindly, and offer a small idea. Perhaps you could share the cleaning or use the leaves as compost for plants.
Compost is a nice thought. I'll ask Mom about it.
Compost is a great use for leaves. They turn into rich soil for plants over time, which is a nice thing to share with a friendly neighbour.
My shoes squeak loudly on the classroom floor. Everyone turns to look.
That can be embarrassing, but it's only a noise. Often the sole is damp or smooth.
Is there a way to stop it?
Dry the soles well, and rub them lightly on a rough mat. A little baby powder inside the shoe sometimes helps. If it continues, a shoe shop can look at it.
My friend borrowed a pen and lost it. It was a gift from my grandfather.
That must be upsetting. Does your friend know it had special meaning?
No, I never told her.
Then it's fair to tell her calmly. Say the pen mattered to you, and that you aren't blaming her, and ask her to look for it. A friendly talk usually works better than silence.
My first time trying a dragon fruit tomorrow. How do I eat it?
Cut it in half, scoop out the soft flesh with a spoon, or peel the skin away. The skin is not eaten.
What does it taste like?
It's mildly sweet and juicy, a bit like a very gentle pear with tiny crunchy seeds. Chilling it first makes it more refreshing.
My baby brother just said his first word and it was my name!
That's a lovely moment. Many families remember such firsts for years.
Mom says it sounded more like 'Dee', but I'm sure he meant me.
You may be right, since babies copy the sounds they hear most. Enjoy being his first favourite word, and encourage him to say it again.
It's very windy today and my cap keeps flying off.
Wind can be playful. Does the cap have a strap or adjuster?
There's an adjuster at the back.
Tighten it so the cap fits snugly, and pull the brim down a little in front. If the wind is very strong, holding it with a hand on top does the job.
I'm doing a crossword and I'm stuck on a clue: 'a place for books'.
How many letters are there in the answer?
Seven, and it begins with L.
Library fits, with seven letters and starting with L. Check the crossing letters to make sure it works.
I have to tell a joke in school assembly, but I don't know any good ones.
A kind, clean joke works best. How about a simple one, like: why did the student bring a ladder to school? Because she wanted to go to high school!
That's actually funny. Can I use it?
Yes, it's a classic, so it's free to share. Say it slowly and pause before the last line, and the class will probably groan and laugh.
I need a book for a long flight, but I can't decide what to pick.
What do you like to read?
Short stories. I like mysteries too.
Then a collection of short mystery stories would suit a flight, since you can read one in a sitting and stop at any point. Pick a paperback, which is light and easy to pack.
What should I give my dad for his birthday? He says he needs nothing.
People who say that often enjoy small, thoughtful things. What does he like doing?
He likes gardening and reading the paper.
A small plant for his garden, a good pair of garden gloves or a nice mug would fit. A hand-written note inside makes any gift more special.
I need to name my new plant. It's got round leaves.
Round leaves are charming. What kind of mood does the plant give you?
Calm and a bit funny.
How about 'Pebble' or 'Coco'? A name that fits the leaves gets more fun the longer you keep it.
I'm meeting my friend's pets for the first time. She has two cats and a parrot.
A cheerful meeting. Do you know the pets' names?
Only that the parrot is called Mango.
Then say hello to Mango in a calm voice and let the pets come to you. Don't reach into the cage or grab the cats, and ask your friend how each one likes to be greeted.
I twisted my ankle a bit during football and it hurts.
I'm sorry to hear that. Please tell an adult right away and have it looked at, since I can't judge an injury from here.
Mom says to rest it. Can I walk on it?
Resting it is what your mom suggests, so listen to her. I can't tell how serious it is, so a doctor should check it, and they can say whether you can walk on it.
I can't remember my locker number and I'm at the corridor.
That happens to many students. Is there a list or a record in the school office?
Maybe, I'll check.
Ask your class teacher or the school office, and note the number somewhere safe, such as the back of your diary, once you find it.
I'm ordering by myself at a restaurant for the first time and I'm nervous.
A nice step towards independence. Do you know what you'd like?
Probably a masala dosa.
Then you're ready. Say, 'Hello, I'd like a masala dosa and a glass of water, please.' Look at the waiter, speak clearly and say thank you when it arrives.
I'd like to wake up early to jog, but my alarm never works on me.
Many people struggle with that. Where is your alarm placed?
Right next to my pillow.
Move it across the room, so you have to stand up to switch it off. Lay out your clothes the night before, and tell a friend your plan.
My grandmother is learning Ludo from me, and she keeps asking if she can move backwards.
Ha, she is playing by her own rules already. In the usual game, pieces only move forward around the board, so you can explain that gently.
She gets upset when I cut her piece.
Cutting is part of the game, but in a family game you can agree on a softer rule, such as sending the piece back without any fuss. Say it with a smile.
She says I'm being too fast with my moves.
Slow down and say aloud what you're doing, like, 'I rolled a four, so I'll move this piece.' It helps her follow the game and makes it feel more relaxed.
She won a round! She's very proud.
Then she deserves a celebration. A cup of tea and a small cheer are in order, and you can tell the family that she beat you fair and square.
She wants a rematch tomorrow. I think she's hooked.
That's the best sign. Keep the rules friendly, and you may find yourself with a regular Ludo partner.
I've got a pen friend now, a girl from another country. We write letters to each other.
What a lovely way to make a friend. Letters feel special because someone took time to write them.
What should I write in the first letter?
Introduce yourself, your family and what you enjoy. Describe your town and ask her two or three questions about her life.
Her English is a bit different from mine and I may not understand everything.
Keep your sentences short and clear. If something puzzles you, ask her to explain it, and share your own doubts too. You'll learn together.
Can I send her a small gift?
A pressed flower, a postcard of your town or a bookmark would be nice and light. Check postal rules for items you plan to send abroad.
I'll send a postcard of the market near my house.
Good choice. Write the date on the back, and she'll have a nice piece of your town on her wall.
My little brother wants a space-themed birthday, but I don't know how to decorate for it.
A fun theme. Stars, planets and rockets are easy to make from paper. What colours do you have at home?
Dark blue paper, yellow paper and silver foil.
Excellent. Dark blue for the night sky, yellow stars hung from the ceiling and foil for rockets or planets. Hang them at different heights to make it feel deep.
What games can we play?
A treasure hunt for 'moon rocks' could work, hiding small stones wrapped in foil. Another idea is guessing planets from clues.
And food?
Round sandwiches could be 'planets', and a fruit platter can become a star shape. Name each dish after something in space, and the children will enjoy it.
I'll make a countdown for the cake. Three, two, one.
A countdown is a great touch. Let the birthday boy press an imaginary launch button, and the candles go on.
Our class is making a rain gauge for a science project, and we don't know how to start.
A rain gauge measures how much rain falls. Do you have a plastic bottle and a ruler?
We have both.
Cut the top off the bottle, turn it upside down and place it back like a funnel. Mark a scale on the side with the ruler and place it in an open space.
Will it be accurate?
A home gauge will give a fair idea, not a perfect measurement. Keep it level and away from trees or roofs, and read it at the same time each day.
Should we empty it every day?
Yes, after you note the reading. Keep a daily chart on a table with the date and amount, and you'll see patterns over the weeks.
Maybe we can compare it with the weather report.
A good idea, as long as you present both as they are. Small differences are normal and make a nice discussion in your project.
My shy friend wants to join the drama club but she's scared of auditions.
It's great that she wants to try. What worries her most?
Speaking in front of strangers.
Suggest she practises with you first, with a short passage or a few lines. Start small, and then move to a few more listeners.
Should I go with her to the audition?
If the club allows friends to wait outside, your company may calm her. The audition itself she will have to do, but a friendly face outside helps.
What if she doesn't get picked?
Remind her that auditions are one step, and many people try more than once. She could also ask the teacher for feedback.
She seems a bit happier now.
Good. A calm plan and a friend close by often turn a big fear into a manageable one.
I'm going on a student exchange to another country for a month and I'll stay with a host family.
What an adventure. A month in a new home will teach you a lot. How do you feel about it?
Excited, but I worry I'll say the wrong thing.
Be polite, listen carefully and ask when you're unsure. People usually appreciate effort more than perfection.
What should I bring for the family?
A small gift from your region, like sweets, a handicraft or a book of local photographs. Ask the exchange coordinator if there are things to avoid.
What about food? I'm a vegetarian.
Tell the coordinator and the host family before you arrive. Explain it simply and kindly, and thank them for adapting.
I'll mention it in my first email. Any tip for homesickness?
Call home at a fixed, short time, keep a small reminder of home and join family activities. Homesick days pass faster when you're busy and talking to people.
I want to turn my school year photos into a scrapbook.
A lovely keepsake. Do you have photos printed, or are they on a phone?
Mostly on a phone.
Choose around twenty favourites, and get them printed. Sort them by month or event, and pick a theme for each page.
What else can I add besides photos?
Ticket stubs, a pressed leaf, a funny note from a friend or your own small captions. These bring the photos to life.
I have a few notes from classmates. Is it okay to stick them in?
Ask the person who wrote the note first, and then it's fine. Many people will be delighted to be included.
Should I write about each page?
A line or two is enough. What happened, who was there and how it felt. Years later, those small notes will be your favourite part.
I'm volunteering at an animal shelter for the first time on Saturday.
A kind thing to do. Do you know your job for the day?
Cleaning cages and walking dogs, I think.
Wear clothes that can get dirty, closed shoes and carry water. Follow the staff's instructions and ask before touching any animal.
What if a dog pulls on the leash?
Stand still, hold the leash firmly and let the staff know. They can show you how to handle that particular dog.
Is it okay to bring treats?
Ask the shelter first. Some animals have special diets, and treats might upset their stomachs.
I'm a bit worried I'll get attached.
That's natural. It shows you care. The shelter works to find homes for animals, and your help makes their stay better.
My birthday is coming and I'm not feeling cheerful. I don't want a party.
That's all right. Birthdays don't have to be loud. Would a quiet day feel better?
Yes, but my family may be disappointed.
You could tell them kindly, 'I'd like a quiet birthday this year, maybe dinner at home.' Most families understand when they know what you want.
What can I do to make it feel special without a party?
Choose a favourite meal, watch something you enjoy and spend time with one or two people you love. Small things can be more memorable than a crowd.
My best friend wants to visit with a cake.
That sounds comforting. A small visit from someone you trust is a nice way to mark the day.
I think I'll say yes to her.
Wonderful. A friend with a cake is exactly the kind of small, kind celebration that suits a quiet birthday.
We have a debate next week on whether school should start later in the morning.
A good topic. Which side are you on?
For starting later.
Then think of reasons such as sleepier students in the early hours, travel time and how much people can focus. Check one or two facts in a library book or article.
What will the other side say?
They may say that it affects after-school activities and family schedules. Prepare a calm answer to each point.
How do I make my points sound strong?
Use short sentences, give an example and speak slowly. State your main point first and your reason afterwards.
I'll write cue cards. Should I look at them while speaking?
A quick glance is fine, but look at the audience most of the time. Practise enough that the cards are just a safety net.
I've got an English speech competition and English isn't my first language.
That takes courage. What topic have you chosen?
'My Village'. I know it well.
A good choice because you can speak from experience. Plan three parts: where it is, what people do there and what you love about it.
My pronunciation is not perfect.
Few speakers are perfect. Speak slowly, with clear pauses, and practise the words you find hard. Ask a teacher to listen once.
Should I memorise the whole speech?
Learn the structure and key lines rather than every word. That way you can stay natural if you forget a phrase.
I'll add a few Hindi words with their meaning. Is that okay?
Check the competition rules. If allowed, one or two words explained in English can add flavour, but don't use many.
My bicycle has a flat tyre and my dad says we'll fix it together.
That's a useful skill to learn. Do you have a repair kit?
Yes, with patches and glue.
Take the wheel off, remove the tube and find where the air escapes. Pumping it up and listening or dipping it in water shows the leak.
What next?
Rough up the area, apply glue, wait until it's tacky and press on the patch. Let your dad show you each step, since tools can be tricky.
Then I put it back?
Check the inside of the tyre for a thorn or nail first, or the new hole will come back. Then replace the tube, pump gently and check the pressure.
Good tip. My dad will be pleased that I'm learning.
He will be, and you'll never be stuck by a flat tyre again. Practise it a couple of times with him watching, and you will be quick at it.
We're planning a day hike and I'm in charge of snacks.
A good job. Think of food that's light, doesn't spoil easily and gives energy. How many people are coming?
Six of us.
Fruits like bananas or apples, nuts, roasted chana, and small sandwiches work well. Pack water for everyone.
Any foods to avoid?
Skip anything that spoils quickly in heat, such as creamy sweets, and anything very messy. Ask the group about allergies.
How should I pack it?
Use small containers or reusable bags, and keep the heavy things at the bottom of the backpack. Carry a small bag for rubbish and bring it all back with you.
I'll also pack a few extra snacks for emergencies.
That's sensible. A small reserve, plus plenty of water, keeps everyone comfortable.
I get nervous when the teacher calls on me, even when I know the answer.
That is a very common feeling. What happens when you're called?
My mind goes blank and my face feels hot.
Before you answer, take a slow breath and say, 'Let me think.' That gives you a couple of seconds, and you can begin.
What if I give a wrong answer?
Then you've learned something, and so has the class. Teachers expect mistakes, and they usually appreciate that you tried.
I'll practise with my sister listening.
Good plan. Ask her to quiz you in different orders, so the questions feel less predictable.
I'm planning a surprise visit to my friend who is in a different town. Is that a good idea?
Surprises can be lovely, but people also need to be ready for visitors. Does she usually like surprises?
She does, but she may be busy.
Then maybe check with someone close to her about her schedule. You can still keep the exact time a surprise.
I can ask her sister.
Good thinking. Ask her sister to keep it quiet, and pick a time when your friend is likely to be at home.
What should I bring?
Something simple she likes, such as her favourite snack or a small plant. Your company is the main gift.
My mango lassi turned out lumpy, not smooth.
Lumps are annoying. Which ingredients did you use?
Mango pieces, curd, sugar and ice.
The ice may not have blended enough, and the mango pieces might be fibrous. Blend longer, and try using ripe, soft mango.
Should I strain it?
You can, with a sieve, though a good blend should be smooth already. Start the blender slowly, then increase the speed.
It's better now. It needs more sweetness though.
Add sugar a little at a time and taste each time. Ripe mango often makes it sweet enough, so go slowly.
I've joined a running group, but they run much faster and I keep falling behind.
That can feel discouraging. How long have you been running?
A few weeks.
That is early days. Tell the group you are new and ask about a slower pace or a beginner's route. Many groups welcome that.
What if they say no?
Then run your own pace and meet them at the end. You could also find another group that suits beginners.
Should I run with them every day?
Not necessarily. Three days a week with rest days in between is gentler on your body. Increase gradually.
I've received feedback that I speak too softly in meetings.
Thanks for sharing that. Feedback like this is something you can practise. Do you feel comfortable speaking up?
Not always. I worry about interrupting.
Try preparing one point beforehand and saying it early in the meeting. Sit up straight, breathe in and speak a little louder than usual.
How do I know if it's loud enough?
Ask a friendly colleague to signal you, or practise at home in a room with the door closed. Aim to be heard by the person farthest from you.
I'll ask my desk neighbour for a thumbs-up if I'm too soft.
That is a gentle signal system. In a few weeks, it will feel natural.
My sister and I want to read one book a month and then talk about it.
That sounds like a good tradition. How will you pick the books?
We could take turns choosing.
Taking turns is fair. Each of you can pick something the other may not have chosen, which widens your reading.
What do we do if one of us doesn't like the book?
Talk about why. Disagreement makes good conversation, and you may see something in the book that the other missed.
Can we do it over tea?
Yes, a tea-and-book evening sounds perfect. Mark the date on the calendar, so it doesn't slip.
I want to make a tiny garden in a jar. Is it difficult?
A jar garden is a manageable project. What kind of jar do you have?
A large glass jar with a wide mouth.
Put a layer of small stones for drainage, then a layer of soil and a small plant that likes humidity. A bit of moss on top makes it look nice.
Do I close the lid?
A closed jar keeps humidity in, but it needs some air now and then. Open it for a short while if you see a lot of water drops on the glass.
Where should I keep it?
In bright light but out of direct sun, because the glass can heat up the plants. A shelf near a window is often right.
I can't decide between two songs for my school singing contest.
What kinds of songs are they?
One is slow and emotional, the other is fast and happy.
Think about which one suits your voice and which you can sing without worrying. Try both in front of a friend and see which one they enjoy more.
I think the slow one fits my voice better.
Then go with the one you can sing with confidence. A well-sung slow song can touch the audience more than a rushed fast one.
What if I feel the audience wants something lively?
Contests are judged on how you perform, not just on how lively the song is. Sing what you do best, and smile as you sing.
We're putting up new curtains and my mother and I disagree on the colour.
A friendly disagreement. What does each of you want?
She likes light yellow, I like dark green.
Bring home small cloth samples of both, and look at them in the room at different times of the day. Light changes colours a lot.
She says dark curtains make the room look smaller.
That's often true for small rooms, but a dark colour can look cosy. Perhaps a lighter shade of green could be a middle path.
A light green might work!
Show her a sample, and see what she thinks. Either way, you'll end up with a colour you both can live with.
I'm having trouble waking up for school and I'm late almost every day.
That's tough, and I can see why it bothers you. What time do you usually go to bed?
Quite late, because I like reading.
Try going to bed a little earlier, in small steps, and keeping a regular wake-up time. Keep your reading to a short time before bed, so it does not push your bedtime later.
Anything else?
Prepare your bag and uniform the evening before, and get some daylight when you wake. If you're still very tired, tell your parents so they can talk to a doctor.
Okay. I'll start tonight with reading for twenty minutes only.
Good plan. Make the change gradually, and see how you feel after a week.
We're hosting our first Raksha Bandhan at home, and I'm in charge of the thali.
A special job. What does your family usually keep on the thali?
A diya, roli, rice grains, sweets and the rakhi.
Then arrange them neatly. Place the diya in the centre, and keep the sweets and rakhi within easy reach. Cover the thali with a clean cloth until it's time.
Should I decorate it?
A few flower petals and a small design on the plate would look lovely. Keep it simple, so it stays tidy.
My brother will be shy about the tilak.
That's fine. A gentle smile and a quick ceremony is enough, and the sweets will cheer him up.
I want to ask my teacher for extra help in maths, but I'm shy.
Teachers are usually glad when students ask. Can you choose a quiet moment, like after class?
Yes, but I don't know what to say.
You could say, 'I'm finding fractions hard. Could you give me a few minutes to go over them?' It's clear and polite.
I'll ask on Monday after class.
Good. Bring your notebook with one example you got stuck on, so your teacher can see exactly where to begin.
My sambar is too sour. What can I do?
Too much tamarind is the usual cause. Did you add much?
A big lump, I think.
Add a small amount of jaggery or a little more cooked dal to balance it. A bit of water and a pinch of salt will help too. Taste after each change.
A spoon of dal worked! It tastes better now.
Well done. Next time, add the tamarind in small amounts and taste as you go, which keeps you in control.
My little sister saved over my homework file by mistake.
That's upsetting. Does your computer keep older versions or a recycle bin?
I'm not sure how to check.
Right-click the file and look for an option to see earlier versions, or check any copy you may have emailed or saved on a pen drive. Ask an adult to help if you're unsure.
I found an older copy on my pen drive. It's most of the work!
Good news. Copy it back to the computer and finish the rest. From now on, keep a backup of your work in another place.
My kho-kho team keeps arguing about who sits first.
Arguments over turns are common. Is there a fixed order?
No, everyone just shouts.
Draw names from a bag or take turns in a written order, and agree to follow it for the whole season. A rule that is fair and written down saves a lot of time.
We'll make a list on a chart. Thanks!
A good plan. Put the chart where everyone can see it, and let each player add their name.
My friend invited me to her house, but her family doesn't speak much English and I only speak English and a little Hindi.
A thoughtful worry. Do you know any words in her family's language?
Just hello and thank you.
Those are enough to start. Smile, greet everyone, and say thank you. Your friend can help with translation, and gestures work well too.
I'll ask her to teach me two more phrases first.
Good idea. Two extra phrases will mean a lot to her family, and they will enjoy hearing you try them.
There's a lot of dust in the air these days and my eyes itch.
That sounds uncomfortable. Is it worse outdoors?
Yes, on the way to school.
It's worth telling your parents so a doctor can look at it if it continues. I can't tell what is causing the itch from here.
I'll tell Mom today. Thanks.
Good. Dust can irritate eyes, so it's sensible to have it checked if it carries on, and your mother will know best what to do.
My cousin and I share a room during the holidays, and he plays music while I sleep.
That's difficult. Have you told him it's bothering you?
Not yet.
Tell him kindly. For example, 'Could you use headphones after nine? I get sleepy early.' Most people agree when asked politely.
What if he forgets?
A gentle reminder the next night is enough. If it keeps happening, ask your parents to help you both agree on a rule.
I'm late for a meeting because the train was delayed. Should I explain?
A short note is enough. What is the meeting about?
A weekly team update.
Send a quick message such as, 'Sorry, my train is delayed. I'll join in about fifteen minutes.' It is clear and professional, with no long excuse.
I sent it. Thanks for the help.
That was the right thing. When you arrive, join quietly, and catch up on any notes afterwards.
I read the first chapter of a mystery and I can't tell who the main character is.
Mystery stories often hold back details at the start. Which names stand out in chapter one?
A girl called Nisha and an old man named Mr Rao.
Then one of them is likely the main character. The one who sees and solves the puzzles is often the lead. Keep reading and notice whose actions drive the story.
I'll look for the one who asks questions. Good tip.
Good tip. Ask yourself, too, whose secrets the story is slowly uncovering. That often points to the central character.
Tomorrow is mismatched socks day at school. I don't know which to wear!
What fun. Pick two very different ones, such as a striped sock and a plain one.
I have a green sock and a spotted purple one.
That is a cheerful mix. Wear them proudly, and show them off at lunch.
I only have one umbrella and my friend and I are walking home in the rain together.
Then you can share it. Hold it higher in the middle, so both of you stay dry.
We'll get wet shoes though.
True, wet shoes are almost unavoidable in the monsoon. Dry them with newspaper inside when you get home.
I get the hiccups every time I eat too fast. Why does that happen?
Eating fast can make you swallow air, and that may irritate the muscle under your lungs, which causes hiccups. I'm not a doctor, but that's the usual idea.
Is there a trick to stop them?
Many people sip water slowly or hold their breath for a few seconds. Eating more slowly is a good way to avoid them in the first place.
I can't choose a ringtone. I have two songs I like.
Which would you be happy to hear fifty times a week?
The first one is less annoying, I guess.
Choose that one, then. A ringtone you can tolerate after many repeats is a better choice than a song you love, since love can wear thin.
We've got a few pieces of stale bread. Can I make something with them?
Yes, stale bread is good for cooking. You could toast it for croutons, or make a savoury bread upma.
How do I make the croutons?
Cut the bread into cubes, toss them with a little oil and your favourite spices, and bake or toast them in a pan until crisp. They're great with soup.
I have some old toys that I've outgrown. What should I do with them?
You could give them to a younger cousin or donate them. Are they in good condition?
Mostly, yes. A few are broken.
Keep the good ones for donation or passing on, and wash them first. Broken toys can be thrown away safely, or sorted for recycling if possible.
A ladybird landed on my notebook while I was studying outside.
What a pretty visitor. Ladybirds are small beetles with bright shells.
Is it safe to touch?
They're usually harmless, but it's best to let it walk onto a leaf rather than handle it. Wash your hands if you do touch it.
My new teacher's name is quite long and I can't pronounce it.
That's a common problem. The kindest way is to ask the teacher how to say it.
What if I say it wrong again?
Try again slowly, and ask the teacher to repeat it once. Most teachers are happy when students make the effort to say their name correctly.
My aunt is coming for tea. What should I prepare?
Simple is best. Do you know what she likes?
She likes plain biscuits and ginger tea.
Then ginger tea with a small plate of biscuits is perfect. Warm the cups first and serve the tea hot.
I lost my bus ticket and the conductor is coming to check.
Stay calm and tell the conductor politely what happened. Look in your pockets and bag in case it's there.
I found it in my school diary!
Good, that is solved. From now on, keep your ticket in one pocket or card holder, so you can find it at once.
The picture frame on my wall keeps going crooked.
That's annoying. Is it hung with a single nail?
Yes, one nail in the centre.
A single nail lets the frame swing. Use two nails, or stick a small piece of adhesive putty at the bottom corners to hold it steady.
My friend is sick and missing school. Can I bring her homework?
That's a thoughtful idea. Have you asked her family if visitors are okay?
Not yet.
Message her family first, since she may need rest. You could drop the homework at the door and wave, or send it through someone else.
I can't open a jar of pickle. The lid is stuck.
Try running the lid under warm water for a minute, which loosens it a little. Then grip it with a dry cloth.
It opened! Thank you.
Well done. A rubber band around the lid also gives you a better grip next time.
Our football practice got cancelled because of rain, and now we're all stuck indoors.
Rain can ruin plans. Is there a hall or a covered area?
There's a corridor.
Then you could do quiet drills, like passing against the wall or practising footwork around a few markers, such as water bottles. Or you could use the time to watch a match and discuss tactics.
I've lost my place in the book because the bookmark fell out.
That's annoying. Do you remember the last scene?
Roughly. A character was on a train.
Flip through to find the train scene and read from there. It's fine to reread a page or two, and you'll be back in the story soon.
Our team scorer is away this week and the coach asked me to keep the scorebook for a cricket match. I've never done it.
A useful job, and you will learn the game better by doing it. Does the scorebook have columns for each batter and each over?
Yes, there are rows for batters and boxes for each ball.
Then record each ball in its box as it happens. Use a dot for no run, a number for runs scored, and a short letter code for a wicket. Ask the coach which codes your team uses.
What if I miss a ball?
Don't panic. Ask the umpire or the other scorer, and fix it in pencil. It is normal to check with others during a match.
How do I keep track of the total?
Add the runs at the end of each over and write the running total in the margin. That way, a single mistake can't grow unseen.
I made it through the first over without trouble!
Well done. After a few overs, your hand will know the pattern, and you'll be following the game as closely as the players.
Our class is running a lemonade stall at the school fair on Saturday. Any tips for getting customers?

Make the stall easy to notice. A bright sign with the price in big letters helps, and so does calling out a friendly greeting to people walking past. Keeping the line short matters too, so share the jobs among your group.
We can't decide who does what.
Split it into three jobs: one person takes money, one pours, and one talks to visitors. Swap every half hour so nobody gets tired or bored, and write the plan on a sheet so everyone can see it.
Dadi's birthday is next week and the whole family is coming over. What could the cousins do for a surprise?

The cousins could perform a short skit or sing her favourite old song together. A surprise that comes from the heart usually means more than a costly gift. Keep the rehearsal secret by practising when she is resting.
Singing sounds good, but none of us can sing well.
That does not matter much for family. Singing together, even off-key, brings smiles. You could also read out a few funny memories about her instead, one line from each cousin.
We're taking an overnight train to Jaipur next month. I've never travelled that way. What should I know?
Keep your ticket and a photo ID easy to reach, since the ticket checker may ask for both. Learn your coach and berth number before boarding, and check the platform on the station boards on the day.
How do I keep my bag safe while I sleep?

Keep valuables in a small bag that stays close to you while you sleep. Many people also lock the main bag to the seat frame with a chain. Keeping money and documents on your person while you sleep is safer than leaving them in a bag.
How do singers know when they are off-key?

They compare what they sing with a steady reference note, like a tanpura drone, a piano key or a tuner. Trained singers also learn to hear the gap between their voice and the note, and then correct it quickly.
Can a person learn to hear that?
Yes. Ear training grows with practice. Singing slowly along with a reference note, and recording yourself to listen back, helps most people hear small differences better over time.
My neighbour asked me to feed their cat for the weekend. I've never looked after one.
Ask the neighbour for clear instructions before they leave: how much food, how many times a day, and where the water bowl sits. Write it down so you do not have to remember it.
What if the cat doesn't come out to eat?

Do not worry too much. Many cats hide when their owner is away, so leave the food, stay calm and quiet, and check back later. If the food has not been touched for a whole day, message your neighbour to tell them.
My team lost the kabaddi final by one point and I can't stop thinking about it.
That is a painful way to lose. It is natural to replay it, and it shows how much you cared. Try writing down what went well, because there was plenty if you reached the final.
What do I say to the team tomorrow?
Thank them for their effort, name one thing each player did well, and say you are proud of the season. Then talk about what the team could work on next time. Keep it short and warm.
A friend of mine keeps cancelling our plans at the last minute and I'm getting annoyed.
It is fair to feel annoyed. Repeated cancelling can make a person feel unimportant. Before assuming the worst, though, there may be a reason you do not know about.
Should I just stop making plans?
I would talk to them first. Say calmly that you feel let down when plans change late, and ask if something is going on. Their answer will tell you whether to keep trying or to meet less often.
My phone keeps saying the storage is full. I don't know what to delete.
Start with things you no longer need, like old videos, repeated photos and downloaded files you have already used. Videos usually take the most room, so check those first.
I'm scared of losing family photos.

Then do not delete them yet. Copy them to a computer or a cloud account first, and check that they open there. Once they are safe in a second place, you can clear the phone without worry. A family member can help you check.
There's a mango tree outside our house with no fruit this year. Why?
Trees do not fruit every year. A mango tree may rest after a heavy crop, and its flowers can fail if the weather is too cold, too wet or too windy during flowering. Young trees also fruit late.
Will it fruit next year?
It may, but nobody can promise it. If the tree looks healthy, with green leaves and new growth, there is a good chance. A gardener or the local nursery can tell you more after seeing it.
I've been asked to organise the shelf in the living room. It's a complete mess.
Take everything off first, so you can see what you have. Then sort into piles: keep, move to another room, and throw away. Wipe the empty shelf before anything goes back.
Where should the heavy things go?

On the lower shelves, and toward the back. Heavy things up high can be dangerous if they fall, and low shelves are also easier to lift from. Keep light things and things used every day at hand height.
Our teacher wants us to pick a book to read over the holidays. I read slowly, so I'm worried.
Reading slowly is fine, and many careful readers are slow. Pick a book that looks interesting rather than a long one. A short story collection can be easier to finish.
Does reading a little every day really help?
Yes. A few pages every day adds up faster than you would expect, and a daily habit is easier to keep than a big weekend session. Over a few weeks, most people also notice they read more quickly.
It's our first Diwali in a new city and we don't know anyone here yet.
A new place can feel quiet at festival time. Many apartment buildings and neighbourhoods hold small gatherings, so check the notice board or ask a neighbour what is planned.
I'm shy about knocking on doors.
A short, friendly greeting is enough: say you are new and wishing neighbours a happy Diwali. You could also leave a small box of sweets with a note. Most people respond kindly to a welcome.
I start a summer job at a bookshop on Monday and I'm nervous about talking to customers.
Being nervous before a first day is normal. A simple greeting like 'Hello, can I help you find something' is enough to begin. You do not need to know every book.
What if someone asks for a book I can't find?
Say that you will check, and ask a colleague or look it up in the shop's list. Customers like honest help more than guesses. After a week or two, you will know the shelves much better.
I have my first lecture at college tomorrow and I'm not sure what to take.
A notebook and pens are the basics, plus any papers the college sent you. Check the timetable for the room and building too, so you are not looking for it at the last minute.
Do I need to buy all the textbooks first?
Not usually. Many lecturers share a reading list in the first week, and the library may have copies. Wait to hear what is needed before spending money.
What if I get lost on campus?
Ask a senior student or someone at the office. They have been there before and most are happy to point the way. Arriving ten minutes early on day one also leaves time to find the room.
It rained so hard yesterday that our street flooded for a few hours.
That sounds stressful. Heavy rain can flood streets quickly, especially where drains are blocked. Did it get into any houses?
No, but the water was knee-high on the road.
Then it was lucky it stayed outside. After water like that, the road may have loose stones or holes under the surface, so walk carefully for a day or two.
Is it worth telling the local office about the drain?
Yes. Reporting a blocked drain helps them fix it before the next heavy rain. Say the street name, where the water gathered, and how long it stayed.
I just started painting with watercolours. Everything turns into a muddy mess.
Muddy colours are the most common watercolour problem for new painters. It usually comes from mixing too many colours or painting over a layer that is still wet.
Is there a way to avoid that?
Use only two or three colours in a mix, and let each layer dry before the next. Rinse the brush between colours. Clean water and patience matter more than the cost of the paints.
How do I make a light colour like pale yellow?
Use a lot of water and only a little paint. Watercolour has no white, so the white of the paper shows through, and more water means more of the paper shows.
I have a science project on how plants grow and I don't know where to begin.
Start with one clear question you can test, such as whether a plant grows differently with more or less light. Then you only change one thing at a time.
I picked light. What do I do next?
Prepare two or more identical plants and give them the same water and soil. Place one where it gets plenty of light and the other where it gets less. Measure the height of each every few days.
How do I show the results?
Draw a simple chart with the days along the bottom and the height going up the side, one line per plant. Then write two or three sentences saying what you noticed and what you think caused it.
Can you help me plan a dinner for four friends who are visiting on Friday?
Happy to help. Do any of them have foods they cannot eat, and how much time do you have to cook?
One is vegetarian and I have about an hour.
Then make a meal that is vegetarian for everyone, so you cook only one thing. Vegetable pulao with raita and a salad is simple and fits in an hour.
That sounds good. What about dessert?
Something that needs no cooking on the day works well, such as fruit with a little honey or a dish you set the night before. That leaves you free to enjoy the visit.
I feel left out because my group made plans without telling me.
That hurts, and it makes sense that you feel left out. It can be even harder when you find out afterwards.
Should I say something to them?
You can, calmly and without blaming. You might say, 'I heard about the plan afterwards and felt left out. Could you tell me next time?' It gives them a chance to explain.
What if they say it was nothing?

You can still say that it mattered to you. Then watch what happens next. If they include you after that, it was likely a slip. If it keeps happening, spend more time with people who make room for you.
Our neighbourhood wants to clean up the park near us. Where do we start?
First talk to the local office or park caretaker, so you know what is allowed and who can collect the waste. Then pick a date and tell neighbours.
How many people do we need?
A small group is enough for a first clean-up. Ten people can do a lot in two hours. Divide the park into sections so that everyone has a clear area.
What about the rubbish we collect?
Ask the office in advance how it will be taken away. Separate it into dry and wet waste when you can. People should also wear gloves and closed shoes, and children should stay with adults.
My cricket coach says I should work on my fielding. I only like batting.
Fielding wins matches, and strong fielders get picked more often. It may help to think of it as the same hand-eye skill you use when batting.
What's a simple drill?

Stand a few steps from a partner and have them throw the ball to you at different heights. Catch it with soft hands, and then throw it back quickly and accurately. Ask your coach for other drills too.
Any way to make it less boring?
Turn it into a game. Count how many catches you make in a row and try to beat that number. Or compete with a teammate to see who has the better throw.
We're thinking of getting a puppy, but our house is small.
Size of the house matters less than time and attention. A puppy needs regular walks, play, training and company, whatever the size of the home.
Who should decide if we're ready?
The whole family together, and especially the adults who will do most of the care. Talk through who will walk it, who will feed it and who will pay for the vet.
Is it okay to adopt instead of buying?
Yes, many animal shelters have healthy puppies and dogs that need homes. Adopting is a kind choice. Staff there can also help you match a dog to your home.
My younger cousin plays video games for hours and my aunt is worried.
Parents often worry about that, and it is good that someone cares enough to notice. Hours of play can crowd out sleep, homework and time outdoors.
Should I talk to my cousin or to my aunt?
Maybe both, separately. With your cousin, be friendly, not bossy, and ask what they enjoy about the game. With your aunt, you could suggest agreeing on daily limits together.
What limit is fair?

There is no single right number. It helps if the limit is agreed in advance and written down, and if homework and meals come first. Your aunt knows the household best, so the decision is hers to make.
We're visiting my grandparents in a village for the first time and the bus ride takes six hours.
Six hours is a long ride, so pack for comfort. Bring water, simple snacks and something to do, such as a book or a music playlist.
I get bored easily on long trips.
Then plan a few small things: a song you want to learn, a game with a family member, or a notebook for drawing. Looking out of the window at the changing countryside can also pass the time.
Will I be able to talk to the village kids?
Probably, if you smile and say hello. Children often find a game to share quickly, even without many words. Asking them to show you their favourite place is a good start.
My mother asked me to learn to make chai properly. I always burn the milk.
Burnt milk usually means the heat is too high or the pot was left alone. Keep the flame at medium and stay beside the pot.
What's the right order?

A common order is water first with tea leaves and spices, then milk, then sugar. Let it rise once, lower the flame, and let it simmer for a short while. Taste it and adjust. Your mother may have her own order, so ask her.
Why does the milk rise so suddenly?
Hot milk forms small bubbles under a thin skin on top. The skin traps steam, so the milk puffs up and spills over when the bubbles get large. Stirring or lowering the flame keeps it down.
I read a mystery novel and guessed the ending too early. Is that a bad sign for the book?
Not always. Some mysteries leave clues on purpose, and guessing right means you read carefully. It can also mean the plot was too easy to predict, though.
How can I tell which it was?

Ask whether the story still surprised you in some way, such as how the reason came out. If you were bored from the moment you guessed, the book probably was predictable. If you enjoyed seeing the clues fit, it worked.
Can you suggest what kind of book to try next?
I cannot tell your taste yet. If you enjoy clues, you might try a classic detective story or a puzzle book. Ask your school librarian too. They often know what readers liked after mysteries.
I forgot my homework at home and the teacher is strict. I'm scared.
That is a tough start to the day. The best step is to tell the teacher honestly before class begins, so you are not caught out later.
What do I say exactly?
Something simple: 'I am sorry, I forgot my homework at home. May I bring it tomorrow?' Say it calmly and look at the teacher while speaking.
What if they punish me anyway?
That may happen, and it would be hard. Honesty usually earns more respect than hiding the problem, though. Accept what the teacher says politely, and bring the work the next day.
How do I stop forgetting things?
Pack your bag the night before and check it against your timetable. Keep homework in the same pocket every day. Within a week, it becomes a habit.
My best friend is moving to another city next month.
That is sad news. Having a close friend leave is a real loss, and it is fine to feel upset about it.
We've been friends since we were small.
Then it will feel like a big change. Friendships that old are strong, and they can survive distance, though it takes some effort from both of you.
How do we stay in touch?
Pick a regular time to talk, such as Sunday evenings. Send small updates in between, like photos or funny messages. Plan a visit in the holidays so you have something to look forward to.
Will we drift apart anyway?
Some friends do, and some do not. What matters most is that both of you keep making the effort. Even if it changes, the time you spent together stays real.
Holi is coming up and my parents are strict about playing outside.
Their worry is probably about safety. Many parents feel better when they know where you will be and who you are with.
What can I tell them to convince them?
Tell them the plan: where you will be, which friends are coming, and when you will be back. Offering to share a phone number of a friend's parent shows you are taking it seriously.
They said I can go if I'm home before lunch.
That is a fair deal. A time limit is a good start, and keeping to it will help them trust you with more freedom next year.
How do I protect my clothes and skin?

Wear old clothes you do not mind staining, and use plain colours that are labelled safe for skin. For anything about your skin or eyes, ask a parent or a doctor rather than relying on advice from friends.
My uncle offered me a short job in his shop during the holidays.
A job like that teaches responsibility and gives you a sense of how work feels.
I don't know if I should accept.
Ask yourself whether you have time, whether you would enjoy it, and what your parents think. It is best to discuss it with them before answering.
They think it's fine. How should I behave there?
Treat it like any workplace: arrive on time, listen carefully, and ask when you are unsure. Being family does not mean you can relax the rules. Customers will judge you the same way as anyone else.
What if I make a mistake?
Tell your uncle at once and ask how to fix it. Everyone slips at the start. Hiding a mistake usually makes it bigger than owning it.
Our balcony is empty and I'd love a little vegetable garden there. Where do I begin?
Check first how much sun the balcony gets. Most vegetables need several hours of direct light a day. Then choose a few easy plants to start with.
It gets sun for about half the day.
Half a day is workable. Leafy plants like spinach, mint and coriander grow well with moderate light. Chillies and tomatoes need more, so try those later.
What do I plant in?
Containers with holes at the bottom, so extra water can drain. Fill them with garden soil mixed with compost. Plastic tubs and old buckets also work if you make drainage holes.
How often should I water?

Check the soil with a finger each morning. If the top layer feels dry, water; if it feels damp, wait. In hot weather it may need water daily, and in cool or rainy weather less often, so adjust as you learn how your plants behave.
I have a school concert and I'm singing a solo. My voice shakes when I'm nervous.
That is a normal reaction to nerves. Many performers feel it, even experienced ones. It does not mean you will sing badly.
Is there something I can do to calm down?
Take slow breaths in through the nose and out through the mouth before you go on. Drinking a little water and standing tall can help too.
What if I forget the words?
Practise until you can sing without the page, and then practise a few more times. If you do forget a line, keep going or hum for a moment. Most listeners will not notice.
Should I look at the audience?
You can look at a spot just above their heads or at one friendly face. That feels less scary than meeting many eyes. Choose whichever feels easier.
I have a small budget and I want to buy a birthday gift for a classmate.
A gift does not have to cost much. What does your classmate like?
They like drawing and cricket.
Then a nice sketchbook or a set of coloured pencils would suit the first interest. For cricket, a small poster or a sports magazine could work.
Which is better?
If you are unsure, take the drawing gift. Art supplies are useful whether or not they follow cricket, and people use them for a long time. A handwritten card makes it more personal.
Do I need to wrap it?
It is not necessary, but wrapping makes a gift feel special. Plain paper with a drawing on it costs almost nothing. Add a short message on the card to finish.
I have a bad headache and an exam tomorrow. What should I do?
A headache before an exam is miserable. I cannot give medical advice, so please tell a parent or another adult at home right away and let them decide whether a doctor should see you.
They are out until evening.
Then message or call them now so they know, and tell another trusted adult nearby if there is one. If you feel worse, ask an adult to get you to a doctor.
What about studying in the meantime?
Whether to study or rest is best decided with a parent, who knows how you are feeling. Please ask them when they are back.
I'm anxious about falling behind.
That worry is understandable. One evening off will not undo your preparation. When you feel better and your parent agrees, go through only the most important topics instead of everything.
I saw a bird building a nest on our window ledge. Should I move it?
It is best to leave it alone. Birds are protective of their nests, and moving one could scare the parents away. Watching from a distance is safer for them.
Will it make a mess?
A little, probably. Twigs and droppings may fall. You can wipe the ledge later, once the birds have flown away.
How long until they leave?
It depends on the kind of bird, but often a few weeks after the eggs hatch. I cannot say for your birds. A local bird club or nature centre could tell you more about the species.
Can I feed them?
It is better not to. Wild parents know what to feed the chicks, and human food can harm them. A bowl of fresh water placed at a distance is a safe, kind choice.
I'd like to volunteer at an old-age home on weekends. Is that a good idea?
It can be a very kind thing to do. Many homes welcome volunteers who bring company and conversation.
How do I find a place?
Ask your school, your family or a local community group for homes in your area. You could also visit one with a parent and talk to the person in charge.
What would I actually do there?
It depends on the home. Common tasks are chatting, reading aloud, playing simple games and helping at events. The manager will tell you what is useful and what is not allowed.
Should I take a friend?
If the home agrees, yes. Going with someone makes the first visit less scary and gives you someone to talk to afterwards. Ask the manager first.
Our class has to make a presentation and I've never used slides.
Start with the story, not the slides. Write down three or four main points first, and then give each point its own slide.
How many words should be on each slide?
As few as possible. A short heading and two or three short lines is enough. Your voice should carry the detail, so the slides only remind the audience of the point.
What about pictures?
One clear picture per slide is plenty. Pick images that explain the point, not just decorate it. Make sure they are big enough to see from the back of the room.
How do I stop reading from the slides?
Practise out loud with only the headings in front of you. If you know your points, the slide becomes a prompt. Practise two or three times and you will feel more at ease.
I'm choosing between two subjects for next year and can't decide.
That is a big choice. What are the two subjects, and what do you like about each?
Biology and economics. I like both.
Then think about what each one is like day to day. Biology often involves labs and memorising detail. Economics involves graphs, reasoning and current events. Which kind of work feels more like you?
I think I like reasoning problems more.
That points to economics, but your marks and interests both matter. It may help to look at what the next course involves and where it leads.
Who can I ask?
Your teachers in both subjects, a senior who took each, and your school or college counsellor. Ask them what a typical week looks like. The final decision is yours and your family's.
I have a maths test on Friday and I get very nervous before tests.
Nerves before a test are common. Preparing well usually shrinks them. How much time do you have before Friday?
Three days.
Three days is enough to make a plan. Pick the topics that worry you most and study one each day, with a short revision on the last day.
What should I do on the morning of the test?
Eat something light, pack the things you are allowed to bring the night before, and arrive a bit early. Do not try to learn anything new; look only at notes you already know.
My mind goes blank when I see the questions.
Take a slow breath and read the whole paper first. Start with the question you feel most sure about. Once one answer is down, the others usually start to come back.
What if I run out of time?
Check the clock at the halfway point. If a question is taking too long, leave space and move on, then return to it. Some marks on every question are better than a perfect answer to just one.
My friend borrowed my favourite book a month ago and hasn't returned it.
That can be annoying, especially when the book matters to you. A month is a long time to hold something.
Should I ask for it back?
Yes. It is fair to ask for what is yours. Keep it light, such as saying you would like to read it again this week.
What if they've lost it?
Then you can say you are disappointed but you would rather hear the truth than excuses. They might offer to replace it. Try to hear their side before deciding how you feel.
Is it okay to stop lending them things?
Yes. You can lend carefully, or only things you do not mind losing. That is not unkind; it is a reasonable limit.
I don't want to ruin the friendship.
A small honest talk usually protects a friendship better than silent anger. Say it kindly, and the friendship will probably be fine.
We're going on a school trip to a fort next week. What should I carry?
A water bottle, a hat and comfortable shoes are the top three. Forts often involve a lot of walking and climbing, and shade can be rare.
Can I take my phone?
Check with your teacher. Many schools have a rule about phones on trips. If it is allowed, keep it in a bag so it does not fall on stone steps.
Should I carry money?
A small amount for snacks or a small souvenir is enough. Keep it somewhere safe, such as an inside pocket, and tell your teacher if something goes missing.
What if I get separated from the group?
Stay where you are and stay calm. Ask a staff member or another adult nearby to help you contact your teacher. Learn your teacher's number before you go.
Is it okay to climb on the walls for photos?
No. Old walls can be unsafe, and many sites forbid it. Take photos from the paths instead. Your safety is more important than a picture.
My grandfather is visiting, and I'd like to teach him how to video call.
Start slowly, because new tools can feel confusing.
He gets frustrated quickly.
Then keep the first lesson short, with only one thing to learn: how to answer a call. Let him press the button himself, so he feels in control.
What if he forgets the steps?
Write them on a card in large letters and keep it near his chair. Short steps, like 'tap the green button', work best. Repeat the lesson a few times over several days.
He says he's too old to learn.
You can tell him that many people learn it later in life, and that the call is for talking to the family, not for the phone itself. Calling a grandchild is a strong reason to try.
How do I stay patient?
Remember how long it took you to learn something new. Take breaks, praise small wins, and let him set the pace. The time together matters more than the lesson.
My sister's birthday is coming and I'm planning to bake her a cake, though I've never baked.
Start with a simple recipe, such as a plain sponge or a one-bowl cake, and read it through twice before starting.
What if it comes out flat?
A flat cake is often due to old baking powder, too much stirring or an oven door opened too early. Measure carefully and follow the recipe exactly the first time.
Should I do a practice cake first?
If you have time, yes. A trial run shows you what to change and builds confidence. A practice cake can be a treat for the family too.
Can I ask an adult to help?
Definitely. An adult can handle the oven and sharp tools safely, and also give advice. Baking with someone else is more fun.
How do I decorate it simply?
Spread a thin layer of cream or icing and add fruit slices or a few sprinkles. Write her name on top with a piping bag or a spoon tip. A neat simple cake looks lovely.
Swimming lessons are starting soon, but deep water scares me.
Fear of deep water is understandable, and it is wise to respect water. Learning with a trained instructor is the safest route.
The pool has a shallow end. Can I practise there?
Yes, shallow water is a good place to build comfort, as long as an adult or instructor is nearby. Never swim alone, even in the shallow end.
What should I practise first?
Ask your instructor, but most beginners start with breathing out underwater, floating and kicking. These are the basis for every stroke.
How long until I'm comfortable?
It varies from person to person. Some take weeks and some take months. Regular lessons and patience matter more than speed.
Should I tell the instructor I'm afraid?
Yes. A good instructor wants to know and will go at your pace. Being honest about fear helps them keep you safe and confident.
Monsoon is starting, and my school books get damp on the way every year.
Damp books are a common problem in the rains. A waterproof cover helps most. Does your bag have a rain cover?
No, it doesn't.
A plastic cover or a large plastic bag works. Put the books in a smaller plastic bag inside the school bag as well, for a second layer.
What if the books do get wet?
Open them carefully and let them air-dry flat in a place with moving air, away from direct sun. Do not close wet pages, and ask a parent or teacher about replacing anything badly damaged.
My shoes are always wet too.
Carrying a spare pair of socks in a plastic bag helps. At home, let the shoes dry in a shaded, airy spot instead of direct sun, which can damage them.
It's tiring planning for all this.
A short checklist by the door makes it automatic: rain cover, plastic bag, spare socks. After a few days, you will do it without thinking.
My phone fell and the screen cracked. Should I buy a new one?
Not necessarily. A cracked screen can often be repaired for less than a new phone. It depends on how the phone works and what repair costs.
How would I know?
Ask a repair shop for a price and compare it with the cost of a new one. Ask whether the repair comes with a guarantee. Get two quotes if you can.
Is a cheap repair shop safe?
Some are, but check reviews from people you know and ask what parts they use. Keep personal information off the phone or back it up before handing it over.
Should I ask my parents?
Yes, especially since the money is probably theirs. Explain what happened honestly and show them the repair quotes. They will appreciate that you did the research.
How can I stop it from cracking again?
A sturdy case and a screen protector help a lot. Avoid keeping the phone in a back pocket or near the edge of a table.
My dog barks at every visitor and it's embarrassing.
Barking at visitors is natural for many dogs, because they guard the home. It can be improved with patient training.
How do I begin?
Teach a calm command like 'sit' or 'quiet', and reward the dog with a treat when it follows. Practise when no visitors are there, then with a family member acting as a visitor.
How long will it take?
It differs from dog to dog. Some learn in a few weeks, others in months. Short daily practice works better than long sessions.
Should I shout at the dog?
No. Shouting can make the dog more excited or fearful. Keep your voice calm and your praise warm when it behaves.
Is a trainer worth it?
A trainer can help if progress is slow or the barking looks like fear or anger. Ask a local vet clinic or animal shelter for trainers they trust.
I'd like to learn chess properly. Where do I start?
Begin with the basics: how each piece moves, how a game starts, and how checkmate works. Many free guides and books explain these for beginners.
I know how the pieces move.
Then learn a few opening ideas: control the centre, bring out your knights and bishops early, and protect your king. You do not need to memorise long lines yet.
How do I get better quickly?
Play regularly and review your games afterwards, especially the lost ones. Spotting your own mistakes teaches more than just reading about strategy.
Can I play against someone stronger?
Yes, losing to a stronger player is a good way to learn. Ask them to explain a few moves after the game, if they are willing.
What about puzzles?
Short tactical puzzles are great for training your eye. A few every day will help you notice captures and threats earlier.
I'm struggling to focus when I study at home. There are always distractions.
Many students have the same problem. Home has its own pulls, such as chores, noise and screens. What distracts you most?
My phone and my younger siblings.
For the phone, put it in another room or on silent while you study. For your siblings, agree on a study time with the family and a place where you work.
What if they won't listen?
Ask a parent to help set the rule, so it is not just you asking. Siblings often respect a family rule more than a request from one person.
How long should I study at a stretch?
Many people work well in blocks of about thirty minutes with a short break after each. Find what suits you. Stand up and stretch during the break.
Does a timetable help?
Yes. A simple timetable lets you plan what to study and when, and it makes starting easier. Keep it short and realistic, so you can actually follow it.
Our power goes out for hours most evenings and I can't finish my homework.
That is frustrating. Planning around the outage can help. Do you know roughly when it usually happens?
Usually between six and eight.
Then do the written work before six, while it is still easy to see. Keep the outage hours for tasks that need no writing, like revising aloud or going over notes in your head.
What if it happens at other times too?
Keep a short list of low-light tasks ready, such as memorising poems or tables. You could also ask a family member how they usually manage in the evenings.
Could I study at a friend's house?
If your parents agree, yes. Arrange it in advance with the friend's family and tell your own family where you will be and when you will come back.
The teacher won't understand if I'm late with homework.
Teachers often do when they hear the reason, especially if you explain it early. Tell them before the deadline, politely, and say when you can hand it in. Bring a plan with you, not only the problem.
Quick question: how do beginners usually learn to juggle?
Most start with one ball, tossing it from hand to hand in a smooth arc at about eye height. When that feels easy, add a second ball, and only then try three.
Why do my throws keep going forward?
That usually means you are releasing the ball too far in front of you. Try to throw it straight up, with your elbows close to your sides, so it lands back in your hand without you stepping after it.
Tabla lessons start tomorrow. Does the order of the first few beats matter?

Yes, in tabla the order and the sounds both matter, because each stroke has its own bol, or spoken syllable, and a rhythm is built by joining them. Your teacher will first show you how to produce clean, clear strokes.
Why do teachers make you say the bols aloud?
Saying the bols helps your mind remember the pattern before your hands play it. It also makes it easier to correct mistakes, because you can hear where the pattern went wrong.
Is it normal to feel sore after the first day of football practice?
Many people notice it after starting something new, but I cannot judge your body. Tell a parent and your coach how you feel, and ask a doctor if you are worried.
My friends say I should skip tomorrow's practice.
That decision belongs to you, your parents and your coach together, not to friends. Tell the coach how you feel before practice starts, and they can adjust what you do.
Why does bread go stale faster in the fridge than on the counter?
The fridge's cool temperature makes the starch in bread harden more quickly. This is why bread often feels dry and firm there, even though cold slows mould.
Then where should I store it?
In a closed bag or box at room temperature for a day or two. If you will not use it soon, you can freeze slices and warm them when needed.
Priya just started her first job and wants to ask for help, but feels silly doing it.
Asking for help early is a sign of good judgement. Everyone at a new job has questions, and colleagues expect them.
How should she ask without seeming lost?
By being specific. She can say what she has already tried and what exactly she is stuck on. That shows effort, and it helps the other person answer fast.
Our flight has a three-hour layover in a big airport. How should we spend it?
Check your next gate early, then relax. A three-hour gap leaves time to eat and rest. Whether you can leave the airport in that time is another matter.
Can we leave to look around?
That depends on your tickets, visa rules and the length of the queues, and I cannot check those. Ask the airline or the airport's information desk before deciding, and keep a margin for the return.
Mr. Kapoor gave us a group project, and one teammate does nothing.
That is a common problem in group work. Before anything else, talk to the teammate in private and ask if something is making it hard to help.
What if they still don't contribute?
Then tell your teacher calmly, with a list of the tasks that are done and the ones that are missing. Teachers can step in and divide the work more fairly.
My laptop takes five minutes to start. Is there a simple fix?
A slow start often comes from too many programs opening at once. Look in the startup settings and turn off the ones you do not need immediately.
What if that doesn't help?
Then check how much free space is left, since a nearly full drive slows things down. If it is still slow, ask someone at a repair shop or a technically skilled family member to look at it.
Why do crows gather in big groups in the evening?
Many crows roost together at night. A big group is safer, since more birds can spot danger, and it may help them share news about where food is. Scientists are still studying the exact reasons.
Do they come back to the same tree?
Often they do. Crows tend to use the same roosting places for long periods, though the group can move if the tree is cut or the birds are disturbed.
I told a joke and nobody laughed, and now I keep thinking about it.
That feels awkward, but jokes fall flat for everybody sometimes. People usually forget such a moment much sooner than the person who told the joke.
How do I stop replaying it?
Try moving your attention to something absorbing, such as a game, a book or a walk. Each time the memory returns, remind yourself that it was a small moment and that it has passed.
My cousins are visiting for a week and our house is small. How do we make room?
Tidy and clear one open area, so people can sit together, and make the sleeping plan early. A simple floor bedding arrangement can work well.
Who decides who sleeps where?
It is best if the adults of the house decide, after hearing everyone's needs. You could suggest that guests choose first, and that you offer to stay flexible.
The local library is closing early on weekdays. Can the neighbourhood do anything?
People can often speak up. Writing a short letter to the library or the local office, signed by many neighbours, shows that people use the place.
What should the letter say?
State the problem briefly, how people use the library, and what change you would like. Be polite, include names and the area, and ask for a reply. Several signatures give it weight.
Does it matter if I read a series out of order?
It can. Some series are made of separate stories, so order matters little. In others, events build on each other, and a later book can spoil an earlier one.
How can I tell the difference?
Look at the back cover or the first pages of each book. Many books say if they are part of a sequence. A librarian can also tell you quickly.
What if I already started in the middle?
You can keep going, and you may enjoy it. You might miss some background, but you can also read the earlier books afterwards and see the story from a new angle.
Our tap drips at night and the sound keeps everyone awake.
A dripping tap is annoying, and it also wastes water. Usually the cause is a worn rubber washer inside, which a plumber can replace quickly.
Can I fix it myself?
Only if an adult who knows how to do it agrees and supervises. Turn off the water supply first. If you are not sure, it is better to call a plumber than to risk a flood.
Meanwhile, how do I stop the noise?
A temporary trick is to tie a piece of cloth or string around the tap so the drip runs down it silently. It is not a repair, but it helps until the plumber arrives.
We're putting up a stall at the Ganesh festival. What can we sell that isn't too expensive?
Simple things sell best. Think of snacks, small decorations, or handmade items that people can buy on impulse and carry easily.
We have a small budget.
Then pick items made from cheap materials, like paper, cloth scraps or things you cook in large amounts. Calculate the cost for each item before deciding the price.
How do we get people to stop at our stall?
Display things neatly and clearly at the front, with large price tags. A friendly smile and a short greeting do a lot. A small sample, if allowed, makes people curious.
I'm comparing two pairs of shoes, one cheaper and one sturdier. How do I choose?
Think about how often you will wear them and for what. For daily use or walking, a sturdy pair usually lasts longer, so it can cost less over time.
The cheaper pair looks nicer.
Looks matter, but fit and comfort matter more. Try both on and walk around the shop. Uncomfortable shoes tend to stay in the cupboard, however nice they look.
What if my feet are still growing?
Then a cheaper pair may be the sensible option, since you will outgrow either pair soon. Leave a little space at the toe, and check the fit again after a few months.
We have to write a research paper and I don't know where to find good sources.
Start with your college library. Books, journals and the library's online catalogue are usually more reliable than random web pages.
How do I know if a source is trustworthy?
Check who wrote it, whether they give references, and when it was published. Sources from universities, official bodies and well-known publishers are generally safer.
What if two sources disagree?
That is normal in research. Note both views, look for the reason they differ, and say so in your paper. Showing that you noticed the difference makes your work stronger.
My parrot repeats words from the TV. Should I worry?
No, parrots naturally copy sounds they hear often. It is how they bond with the people around them.
Can I teach it new words?
Yes, with patience. Repeat a short word in a clear voice at the same time every day, and praise the bird when it tries to copy. Some take weeks to pick up a word.
Why does it sometimes copy angry voices?
Birds copy sounds that stand out, not because they understand the feeling. If an angry voice is repeated often, the parrot may pick it up. Speaking gently around it helps.
A classmate always copies my homework and I'm not sure how to say no.
Saying no is allowed, since the homework is your work. A calm, clear refusal is usually enough. Does the classmate struggle with the subject?
I think so. They say they don't understand it.
Then you can offer help in another way, such as explaining a topic or studying together. That helps them learn, which copying does not.
What if they get angry?
They might at first. Stay polite and say that you will study with them but will not hand over the answers. If the pressure continues, tell your teacher or a parent.
How do clouds stay up in the sky if water is heavy?

A cloud is made of tiny droplets or ice crystals that are so small and light that they drift. Rising air also helps hold them up. When droplets join and grow bigger, they become heavy enough to fall as rain.
Why are some clouds dark?
Thick clouds block sunlight, so their undersides look dark. A cloud with a lot of water and great depth lets very little light through, which is why rain clouds often look grey.
Do clouds weigh anything?
Yes, a big cloud can hold many tonnes of water, so it weighs a lot in total. It stays up because its droplets are so tiny that they fall very slowly, and rising air keeps carrying them back up.
Our school is picking a relay team and I want to try out for it.
That could be a good challenge. Do you know what the selection involves?
They time each runner over a short distance.
Then practise short, fast runs and work on a good start. Warm up properly beforehand, and ask your teacher or coach how to do it safely.
I'm not the fastest in my class.
