Clearly and at a steady pace. Take a breath before answering, and keep your answers short. Ask politely for the question to be repeated if you did not hear it.
What should I wear?
Neat, comfortable clothes that suit the setting. Being comfortable helps you feel confident.
How do people's passwords get stolen?
The most common ways are fake emails or sites that trick people into typing them, data leaks from sites that were hacked, and malware that records keystrokes.
Which is the most common?
I cannot give exact numbers, but fake messages, called phishing, are among the most common. They work because they look genuine.
How do I protect myself from phishing?
Do not click links in unexpected messages. Go to the site yourself by typing its address, and check the sender carefully before sharing anything.
Does a password manager help?
It can. It creates and stores different strong passwords, so one leak does not expose all your accounts. Protect the manager with one strong password.
How should I store vegetables so they last longer?
Different vegetables need different care. Leafy greens last longer wrapped in a paper towel inside a container. Root vegetables like potatoes and onions prefer a cool, dark, dry place.
Should onions and potatoes be kept together?
No. They give off moisture and gases that can make each other spoil sooner. Store them in separate places with good airflow.
What about tomatoes?
Ripe tomatoes keep their flavour best at room temperature, away from direct sun. Once they are very ripe, the fridge slows spoilage, though it dulls the taste.
How can I tell when a vegetable has gone bad?
Look for mould, a slimy surface, a sour smell or very soft patches. When in doubt, throw it out.
I'm going to a city where I don't speak the language.
Learn a few key phrases, such as hello, thank you, please and how much. Locals usually appreciate the effort.
What if I get lost?
Keep the address of your stay written in the local language, and use an offline map. You can also show the address to a shopkeeper or a driver.
How do I order food?
Point at the dish on the menu or on another table, or use a translation tool. Pictures on menus help a lot.
What if I need real help?
Find the address of your country's embassy or consulate, or the local emergency number, before you travel and keep it somewhere safe.
I'm always worried about letting people down.
Many people feel that. It often comes from caring about others and wanting to do well. When does it feel strongest?
When someone gives me a task.
Try asking exactly what they expect and when. Clear expectations remove a lot of the guesswork that makes you anxious.
What if I can't do everything?
Say so early and suggest what you can do. Most people prefer honesty to a surprise at the last minute.
Will the worry ever go away?
It can ease with practice, as you see that honest limits do not ruin relationships. If it stays heavy, a counsellor can help you work through it.
How do I run a short team meeting well?
Share the agenda in advance, and keep to the time. Start with the most important item so that you cover it even if time runs short.
What if people go off-topic?
Gently note the point and say, 'Let's come back to that after,' and write it down for later. Then return to the agenda.
How do I make sure everyone speaks?
Ask quieter members directly for their views, and invite input round the table. Thank people for contributing.
What should happen after the meeting?
Send a short note with decisions and who will do what by when. This keeps everyone on the same page.
Why does the sea have tides?
Mostly because of the moon's gravity. It pulls on the ocean, creating a bulge of water on the side facing the moon, and another on the opposite side.
Why twice a day?
The Earth rotates through those two bulges roughly once a day, so most coasts see two high tides and two low tides daily.
Does the sun matter?
Yes, it also pulls on the oceans, but less than the moon. When the sun and moon line up, at new and full moon, the tides are especially high.
Do lakes have tides?
They do in a tiny way, but the effect is too small to notice. Tides are visible mainly in the oceans.
What's the best way to warm up before playing a sport?
Start with a few minutes of light movement, such as jogging or skipping, to raise your heart rate. Then do gentle dynamic stretches like leg swings and arm circles.
Should I hold stretches for a long time?
Before play, moving stretches are usually preferred over long static holds. Static stretching is often saved for after exercise.
How long should a warm-up be?
Around ten minutes is a common suggestion, though it depends on the sport and the weather. Cooler days need more time.
What if something hurts during it?
Stop and rest. For a pain or injury, see a doctor or physiotherapist, as I cannot advise on that.
I'd like to try pottery.
A beginner class at a local studio is the best way to start. You can try hand-building techniques, like pinch pots and coils, before moving to the wheel.
Is the wheel harder?
Most people find it harder at first. Centring the clay takes practice, so give yourself time and expect plenty of wobbly bowls.
How is the clay made hard?
It is dried and then fired in a kiln, which is a very hot oven. Studios usually fire your work for you, so you do not need your own kiln.
Will I need special clothes?
Wear something you do not mind getting dirty, and keep your nails short. An apron helps, and many studios supply them.
We want to organise a clean-up of our local park.
Start by getting permission from whoever looks after the park, and agree on a date. Then gather volunteers and tell neighbours about it.
What should we bring?
Gloves, sturdy bags, litter pickers if you have them, and water. Closed shoes protect feet from sharp objects.
What about the glass or sharp things?
Collect these in a separate sturdy container, and handle them carefully. Keep young children away from them.
How do we get the rubbish taken away?
Contact the local municipal office before the day, so they know where to collect it. Sort recyclable items if a facility is available.
What makes a good detective story?
A puzzle that the reader can follow, clues that are placed fairly, and a surprising but logical solution. Interesting characters add to the fun.
What's a 'red herring'?
It is a false clue that leads the reader, and often the detective, in the wrong direction. Writers use it to keep the mystery alive.
Is it better if the reader can guess the ending?
The best stories let attentive readers solve it just before the reveal, or leave them thinking, 'I should have seen that.' Too obvious feels dull, and too random feels unfair.
Are there good Indian detective characters?
Yes. For example, Feluda, created by Satyajit Ray, is a beloved Bengali detective. His stories have been translated into many languages.
What do people eat at Onam?
The main meal is the Onam sadya, a feast with many vegetarian dishes served on a banana leaf. It includes rice, sambar, avial, thoran, pickles, pappadam and sweet payasam.
Is there an order to eat in?
Yes. Dishes are placed in set positions on the leaf, and the meal usually begins with rice and parippu or sambar, moves on to payasam, and ends with rice and buttermilk.
Do people eat with their hands?
Traditionally, yes. People eat a sadya with the right hand. Fingers are used to mix the rice with the curries.
Is it eaten on the floor?
Traditionally, many families sit on mats on the floor. These days, tables and chairs are also common, especially in restaurants.
I can't focus in online classes.
Online classes make it easy to drift, with many things competing for your attention. What usually distracts you?
My phone, mostly.
Put it out of reach or in another room during class. Turning off notifications helps if you must keep it nearby.
What about taking notes?
Taking notes by hand or in a document keeps you active. Write down questions as they come up and ask them at the end.
What if the lecture is too fast?
Ask if the recording will be shared, so you can replay parts. You can also ask the teacher to repeat key points.
Should I turn my camera on?
Follow your teacher's rules. If you can, keeping it on may help you feel more engaged, and it can help a teacher see who is following.
I'd like to ask my team for feedback but I'm not sure how.
Ask specific questions. 'What is one thing I could do better in meetings?' gets more useful answers than 'Any feedback?'
Who should I ask?
People who see your work closely, such as teammates you often work with, a senior colleague or your manager.
When is a good time?
After a project or a task is complete, or in a one-to-one chat. Choose a quiet moment, not a rushed one.
What if the feedback is hard to hear?
Listen, thank them and take some time before reacting. You do not need to agree with everything, but look for patterns.
What should I do with it?
Choose one or two points to work on, and tell the person you will try them. Following up later shows you valued their view.
I feel like my friend and I are drifting apart.
It happens when lives change. Sometimes it can be fixed with a little effort. Do you want to stay close?
Yes, but we talk less now.
Reach out with a simple message about something you shared, like a memory or a joke. Small, regular contact helps more than a big gesture.
What if they don't reply?
They may be busy. Wait a few days, and try once more. If the effort is one-sided for a long time, it may be worth accepting a different kind of friendship.
Should I suggest meeting up?
Yes, a specific idea works better than 'let's meet sometime'. Suggest a day and a place, like a walk or a cup of tea.
What if we have nothing in common any more?
You may still enjoy catching up on each other's lives. Ask about what they care about now. Friendships can change shape and still be real.
My laptop battery drains very fast now.
Batteries wear out over time, and each full charge uses up a little of their life. Bright screens and many open programs also drain power.
How can I check its health?
Many laptops have a battery report or health page in their settings. It shows how much capacity is left compared with when it was new.
Can I save power in the meantime?
Lower the screen brightness, close programs you are not using and switch on the battery saver mode if there is one.
Is it fine to leave it plugged in all day?
Many modern laptops manage this well, though heat is bad for batteries. Keep the laptop cool and check the maker's advice for yours.
When should I replace the battery?
When it no longer lasts long enough for your needs, or the health report shows very low capacity. A repair shop or the maker's service centre can fit a new one.
Next month I'm flying for the first time.
Check your ticket for the departure time and the airline's baggage rules, and carry a valid photo ID.
What happens at the airport?
You check in, drop off your big bag, go through security and then wait at your gate. Signs and staff show the way at each step.
What can't I take in my cabin bag?
There are limits on liquids and some sharp or dangerous items. The airline and airport websites list what is allowed, so read them before you pack.
What if I miss my flight?
Contact the airline straight away. Whether you can be rebooked depends on their rules, so arriving early is the best protection.
Is it normal for the ears to feel strange during take-off?
Yes, many people notice pressure in their ears. If it bothers you or you have a health concern, ask a doctor before you travel.
We're planning a picnic. What should we make?
Pick food that stays good without refrigeration and is easy to eat, such as sandwiches, wraps, fruit and boiled eggs. Keep drinks cold in a bottle or a cooler.
What about food that spoils quickly?
Keep it cool, and eat it early. Items with curd, cream or cooked rice can spoil quickly in the heat, so keep them in an insulated bag with ice packs or skip them.
How do I carry it all?
Use sealed containers inside a sturdy bag, and pack heavy things at the bottom. A cloth to sit on and a bag for rubbish are useful.
Should we bring games?
If you like. Cards, a frisbee or a ball are easy to carry. Pick a spot with shade and enough space.
How do we leave the place?
Take all your rubbish with you, including food waste. Leave the spot cleaner than you found it.
I want to feel more confident around people.
Confidence tends to grow with practice. Start in small, comfortable situations, then build up. What feels hardest?
Starting conversations.
Begin with a simple remark or question about something around you, such as the event or the place. People often respond warmly to a friendly opener.
What if the conversation dies?
Ask an open question like 'What did you enjoy about it?' Everyone has silences. It is fine to end politely and move on.
I always think they find me boring.
Most people are focused on how they come across, not on judging you. Showing real interest in what they say is more attractive than being impressive.
How long will it take?
It varies. Small steps over weeks and months make a noticeable difference. If shyness feels overwhelming, a counsellor can offer more support.
We want to start a Sunday cricket match in our neighbourhood.
Find a safe open space, and ask whoever looks after it for permission. Then invite people through notices or the residents' group.
How do we make teams fair?
Let two captains take turns choosing players, or mix ages and skills so both sides are balanced. Rotate captains every week.
What if someone argues about a decision?
Agree on simple rules before the first game, such as who umpires and what counts as out. When a dispute comes up, the umpire's decision stands.
Any safety points?
Check the ground for stones and holes, use a soft ball for younger players and keep windows and cars away from the playing area.
How do we keep it going?
Pick a fixed day and time so people can plan, and keep matches short enough for everyone to bat and bowl.
We found a tiny kitten near our gate.
Check first whether it looks well and whether its mother is nearby, since she may return. Keep the area quiet and watch from a distance for a while.
The mother hasn't come back.
Then contact a local animal rescue group or a vet soon. A very young kitten needs specialist care, and I cannot give advice on feeding or treating it.
Can we give it milk?
Please ask the vet or the rescue group before feeding anything. The wrong food can harm a young kitten.
Should we touch it?
Handle it as little as possible, and wash your hands afterwards. The rescue group can tell you how to move it safely.
What if we want to keep it?
That is a big decision. The vet or rescue group can talk about what it needs, such as vaccinations and a home for years to come.
How do trees help a city?
Trees give shade, and their leaves release water vapour that cools the air. They also trap dust and absorb carbon dioxide, and they give birds and insects a home.
Do they really cool things down?
Yes. Streets with trees are often noticeably cooler than bare, paved ones. Shade keeps surfaces from absorbing as much heat.
Are all trees equally good for a city?
No. Native species usually suit the climate and support local wildlife. Strong roots, wide canopies and little litter matter for city streets.
What can one person do?
You can plant a sapling where it is allowed, water young trees nearby and join a local planting drive. Speak up when trees are being cut without need.
How long does a new tree take to grow?
It depends on the species. Some give useful shade in a few years, but many take a decade or more to grow large.
What instrument should a beginner pick?
Choose one that matches the music you love listening to, since you will practise more if you enjoy the sound. Keyboard, ukulele and flute are common beginner choices.
Which is cheapest to start?
Ukulele and recorder or flute can cost less than a keyboard or guitar, though prices vary widely. A used instrument from a friend or shop is another option.
Is it easier to learn one with keys?
A keyboard shows all the notes in order, so many beginners find it clear. A ukulele only needs a few chords to start playing songs.
Can I try before I buy?
Yes. Many music shops let you try instruments, and a teacher or friend may lend one. Trying a few helps you see what suits you.
Do I need a teacher?
Not always, but one can help you build good habits early. Online lessons and books are alternatives if a teacher is not possible.
Should I read a book before watching the film?
There is no rule. Reading first lets you imagine the story your own way, while watching first can make the book easier to follow. It is a matter of taste.
Films usually change things, don't they?
Yes. Films have to fit a story into a couple of hours, so they often cut or merge characters and scenes. Many fans enjoy comparing the two.
Does that mean the film is worse?
Not necessarily. A film is a different art form, and some adaptations improve on the book in places. They just tell the story in a different way.
What if I already know the ending?
Many people still enjoy a story they know, as the pleasure is in how it is told. Look for details and moments that you missed before.
Which should I pick today?
If you have time and enjoy reading, try the book first. If you want a quick taste of the story, watch the film. Either choice is fine.
